title: feat: add noSolderPaste to all SMT pad shapes
description: Adds noSolderPaste?: boolean to the TypeScript interfaces and Zod schemas for every smtpad shape: rect, rotated rect, circle, pill, rotated pill, and polygon, allowing TSX authors to express testprobe pads with exposed copper and no solder paste.
body:
Adds `noSolderPaste?: boolean` to the TypeScript interfaces and Zod schemas for every `<smtpad>` shape: rect, rotated rect, circle, pill, rotated pill, and polygon. This lets TSX authors express test/probe pads with exposed copper and no solder paste, including pads inside footprints.

Related to https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/4630.

The parser accepts only booleans, preserves explicit `true`/`false`, and leaves omitted values undefined. The intended behavior is that `true` suppresses paste independently of solder mask settings and takes precedence over `solderPasteMargin`; omission or `false` preserves existing paste behavior. There are no aliases or migration requirements. Core still needs to consume this prop to suppress `pcb_solder_paste` generation.

Includes tests for all six shapes, omitted and explicit values, coexistence with mask and margin settings, and invalid inputs. Regenerated all required documentation.

Validation: `bun test` (680 passed), `tsc --noEmit`, `biome format .`, and `bun run build` passed.

title: fix: parse explicit polarity pins in diode footprint strings
description: Fixes the parsing of explicit polarity pins in diode footprint strings to ensure correct polarity markings without altering copper pad numbers or retaining supplier artwork.
body:
Explicit polarity modifiers such as `diode_p3.4mm_pw1.2mm_ph0.95mm_rounded0_cathodepin1` throw `Diode cathode pin must be 1 or 2`, although the equivalent numeric builder call works. Footprinter strings pass numeric modifier values as strings; the generic diode generator forwarded them to the fabrication-note helper without normalizing them.

Parse the common options through the existing schema before passing the anode/cathode pins to the helper. This generates the correct polarity markings without changing copper pad numbers or retaining supplier artwork.

The regression covers both modifier names on either physical pin, compares string output with the builder, rejects conflicting polarity assignments, and includes one PCB SVG snapshot.

Validation:
- Confirmed the new regression fails before the change.
- `bun test tests/diode.test.ts tests/diode-fabrication-notes.test.ts tests/sod123w.test.ts` — 41 passed.
- `bun run build` — JavaScript and declarations passed.
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Required by the revised diode-identity solution in tscircuit/cli#5371.

title: feat: honor noSolderPaste on SMT pads and bump props
description: Exposed testprobe pads can now use smtpad noSolderPaste  to omit pcb_solder_paste while keeping copper exposed, affecting all six pad shapes and ensuring proper paste creation checks.
body:
Exposed test/probe pads can now use `<smtpad noSolderPaste />` to omit `pcb_solder_paste` while keeping copper exposed. The shared paste creation check handles all six pad shapes, including polygons and pads inside footprints, on either layer. Omitted or explicit `false` preserves existing behavior, covered pads still emit no paste, and `true` takes precedence over `solderPasteMargin`.

Bumps `@tscircuit/props` and its override from `^0.0.701` to `^0.0.703`, which includes tscircuit/props#938.

Fixes #4630.

Adds a labeled PCB snapshot and a 72-pad regression matrix covering all six shapes on both layers, omitted/false/true values, margin precedence, and covered pads. Assertions check the emitted paste records and preservation of copper, mask coverage, and mask margins.

Validation:
- 23 focused SMT pad, solder paste, testpoint, solder mask, and USB-C tests pass.
- `tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, distribution smoke tests, and formatting pass.
- All ten CI test shards pass, together with CI type checking, formatting, package preview, distribution smoke tests, and Vercel deployment.

Dependency availability: confirmed that the published `@tscircuit/props@0.0.703` installs successfully; all 23 focused tests also pass against the npm release.

title: fix: translate rounded board outlines to the resolved board center
description: Fixes alignment of generated rounded board outlines with the resolved board center during rendering, preventing false outside-board errors.
body:
Fixes #4633.

Translate generated rounded board outlines to the resolved board center during initial rendering and auto-sizing. This keeps the outline aligned with `pcbX`/`pcbY` and prevents false outside-board errors.

One regression test directly matches the emitted Circuit JSON: board and component centers at `(10, -10)`, rounded outline points spanning x=5..15 and y=-15..-5, and no errors. No new snapshot files.

Validation: the regression fails before the fix and passes afterward; it and both existing border-radius tests pass (3 tests). Formatting passes. The previously reported broader test failures and cached dependency type conflicts remain local validation limitations.

title: fix: avoid extra built-in terminals when custom symbols declare ports
description: Fixes the issue of extra built-in terminals being created when a custom symbol declares its own ports, preventing false unconnected-pin warnings.
body:
SW4’s custom symbol declares six ports: `1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7`. Core also adds pin4 from the built-in DPDT symbol, causing a false unconnected-pin warning.

This fix prevents extra built-in terminals from being created when a custom symbol declares its own ports. Existing port matching and positioning stay intact. Custom drawings without ports keep the default fallback, and partial `pinLabels` still work.

TSX tests and SVG snapshots cover SW4, drawings without ports, partial pin labels, and genuine unconnected-pin warnings. **12 switch tests and type-checking passed.**

Stacked on the reproduction PR #4644.

title: repro: custom DPDT symbol gains a phantom pin4
description: Fixes the issue where the custom DPDT symbol incorrectly inherits an extra phantom pin4, leading to missing trace warnings.
body:
SW4 (`JS202011JCQN`) has pins **1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7**, but core adds **pin4** from the built-in DPDT symbol and reports `Port pin4 on SW4 is missing a trace`.

The test inlines the project's **exact schematic symbol and pinLabels** from `pico-pd-motor-lab/imports/JS202011JCQN.tsx`: all six ports, original coordinates and stem lengths, seven paths, contact-link markings, reference text and “DPDT • shown OFF” legend are unchanged. An AST comparison against the project verified equality, ignoring formatting.

The test uses the original SW4 wiring from `circuit/power-switch.tsx`: pin1/pin5 to GND, pin2 to POWER_SWITCH_EN, pin3 to POWER_ON_LEVEL, pin6 to ARM_BASE, and only pin7 marked no-connect. The symbol is defined directly in `tests/repros/repro-custom-dpdt-phantom-pin.test.tsx`; there is no separate symbol fixture file. PCB/CAD assets are omitted because this is a schematic/source-port regression.

The native SVG shows the exact symbol, its original net connections, the actual emitted source-pin list and the checker message. Explanatory notes are outside the symbol. The test deliberately asserts the current broken behavior; no production code is changed.

![Exact SW4 symbol: six real terminals but seven generated source ports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/f3d37d1a9bc64c2c4742ce03d02ebecf1b208fd0/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-custom-dpdt-phantom-pin-schematic.snap.svg)

Validation:

- Exact symbol and pinLabels match the project in an AST comparison.
- Repro and existing switch/no-connect tests: 7 passed.
- `bunx --no-install tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- Biome formatting and visual inspection of the generated SVG: passed.

The fix is stacked on this reproduction in #4645.

title: Prefer exact PCB-port route endpoints
description: Prefers exact PCB-port matches for routed endpoints to avoid incorrect source trace attribution when endpoints fall inside adjacent pads.
body: A routed endpoint can land exactly on a PCB port while also falling inside an adjacent pad. Geometry-based attribution collected both candidates and could select the wrong source trace. This prefers exact PCB-port matches before pad containment. The stacked #4632 snapshot naturally removes the connectivity DRC.

title: Repro adjacent-pad trace attribution DRC
description: Fixes incorrect source trace attribution for routed endpoints overlapping adjacent pads in PCB designs.
body: Adds a reduced LMG342X repro where a routed endpoint lands exactly on the FB PCB port while also overlapping the adjacent VOUT pad. The current geometry lookup attributes the route to VOUT, and the PCB snapshot shows the resulting connectivity DRC.

title: fix: honor oval plated-hole rotation during autorouting
description: Fixes autorouting issues by ensuring that oval plated-hole dimensions are correctly rotated and used as routing obstacles during PCB design.
body: A USB-C connector rotated by 90° has correctly rotated oval shield-slot copper, but routing obstacles use its unrotated dimensions. In the merged TSX repro (#4618), both CC traces touch the grounded shield slots. Normalize oval plated-hole outer bounds with the existing quarter-turn rectangle helper: a 2.2 × 3.2 mm slot becomes a 3.2 × 2.2 mm obstacle at 90°/270°. Other angles retain their CCW rotation. Activate the merged repro and update its PCB snapshot; the fixed board routes both CC connections with zero DRC errors. Add a TSX regression and labeled snapshot covering 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°, and 33° on both board sides. Expected quarter-turn bounds come from transformed corners of the emitted hole geometry. Validation: - The edited source converter, wired into the matching published core 0.0.2152 renderer/router, passes the USB-C repro, the new rotation test, and the existing rotated-rectangle routing test. - The unfixed pipeline fails only on the USB-C contact assertion: expected zero contacts, received two. The fixed pipeline produces zero board DRC errors. - Three native source obstacle tests pass: identity preservation, circular via obstacles, and ten-layer drilled obstacles. - Scoped TypeScript checks for the changed converter and TSX tests, Biome 1.9.4, and whitespace checks pass. Full source-checkout tests are blocked locally by the unavailable unpublished `@tscircuit/flex-utils` dependency. The functional validation uses the actual edited source converter with the matching published renderer/router; its harness remains outside the repository.

title: Fix footprint keepouts staying behind after PCB layout
description: Fixes the issue where footprint keepouts do not move with their associated PCB components during layout, allowing copper to intrude into designated clearance areas.
body: PCB grid placement moves a module's pads and notes while leaving its footprint keepout at its initial position, allowing copper into the intended antenna clearance. Emit the owning `pcb_component_id` and actual enclosing `pcb_group_id` for rectangle and circle keepouts so the existing layout utilities move them with their owner. Inside ``, `pcbY={15.8}` is a footprint-local offset, not a fixed board position. The keepout and green note rectangle start with that same offset and should receive the chip's layout translation. Previously the keepout lacked ownership, so layout moved the note rectangle but left the keepout behind. Reuse the existing repro from #4522 and update its existing snapshot. Remove the unrelated pinheader and extra antenna decorations; two grid columns still force the single chip to move. With the original code, the keepout stays at `(0, 15.8)` while the marker moves to `(-26.6, 0.9)`; this fix aligns them. No new tests or dependency changes. Validation: - [GitHub Actions test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/38519476466) passes all 10 test jobs. - CI typecheck, distribution smoke tests, package preview, formatting, and dependency checks pass. - 30 existing keepout, copper-pour, grid, flex, and manual-via tests pass locally. - The simplified keepout regression fails at its position assertion when the original keepout emission is restored. - Biome and `git diff --check` pass. Local tests used an isolated dependency install with published Circuit JSON 0.0.525 and Git sources for dependencies whose archive downloads are blocked in this environment.

title: fix: respect rotated pad geometry when assigning routed source traces
description: Fixes incorrect source trace assignments for routed traces on rotated SMT pads, resolving trace-continuity validation failures.
body: Rotated SMT pads were matched using their unrotated dimensions, so routed INA237 SDA and SCL traces inherited adjacent pins’ source metadata even though their copper reached the correct pads. This fixes the bug reproduced in #4527, which also caused trace-continuity validation failures on the full INA237 board. Endpoints and pad centers are points in board coordinates, measured in millimeters with +X right and +Y up. For `rotated_rect` pads, undo the emitted counterclockwise rotation about the pad’s center using `rotateDEG` and `applyToPoint` from the existing `transformation-matrix` dependency, then apply the rectangular width/height check. This corrects containment for arbitrary rotations and preserves the existing trace-width tolerance. Update the existing INA237 reproduction and annotated snapshot to expect correct ALERT/SDA/SCL associations. Full-board verification with the original footprint string and the board placement corrections from [sparkfun-boards #361](https://github.com/tscircuit/sparkfun-boards/pull/361): the old core produces 50 traces and 29 vias with seven trace-continuity errors; this fix produces the same copper geometry with zero circuit errors and correct sensor pin/net associations. The untouched original board still skips autorouting because U2 overlaps R4 and its courtyard overlaps R2; those placement corrections are required separately. Validation: - 56 existing related routing tests pass (239 assertions), including the INA237 reproduction and opposite-layer attribution coverage. - The updated INA237 reproduction fails against the pre-fix implementation. - Biome and `git diff --check` pass. - Full TypeScript check attempted: restricted dependency downloads required local source checkouts, which report errors in dependency sources and existing schematic consumers. No diagnostics reference the changed files. Dependency declarations are unchanged.

title: repro: KiCad exports omit hierarchical child schematic files
description: Fixes the issue where KiCad exports do not include hierarchical child schematic files, resulting in blank pages when attempting to open them.
body: ## Motivation Multi-sheet tscircuit designs export a KiCad root schematic that correctly names and references every child sheet, but the CLI writes only that root `.kicad_sch` file. The referenced child schematic files are missing from both the KiCad ZIP and the generated project directory. KiCad therefore shows the expected sheet names in the hierarchy panel, while opening a child sheet produces a blank, unsaved page because its `Sheetfile` cannot be found. This makes an existing schematic look empty and prevents users from reviewing or editing the exported sheets. ## Issue ## Reproduction The fixture declares `power` and `control` schematic sheets and assigns one component to each. The CLI integration tests cover both affected paths: - `tsci export index.tsx -f kicad_zip` - `tsci build index.tsx --kicad-project` In both outputs, the root schematic references `power.kicad_sch` and `control.kicad_sch`, but neither child file is written. The converter already exposes the complete hierarchy through `getOutputFiles()`; the CLI paths currently use only `getOutputString()`, which returns the root file.

title: fix: preserve diode identity and polarity in imported footprint strings
description: Fixes the issue where the diode identity and polarity were lost during the import of footprint strings, ensuring accurate representation in the PCB design.
body:
C82046 imports as a generic `smdpads2` string because the CLI omits EasyEDA category tags from footprint-discovery hints. Forward those category strings so the existing matcher selects its copper-equivalent diode candidate and encodes the cathode pin:

```tsx
footprint="diode_p3.4mm_pw1.2mm_ph0.95mm_rounded0_cyw5.1mm_cyh2.2mm_cathodepin1"
```

The copper match remains 99.9953%. Pin labels and the CAD model stay identical. The footprint string generates the diode markings; supplier artwork preservation is outside this change.

Update `@tscircuit/footprinter` to the published `0.0.438` release, which contains the merged numeric-polarity parsing fix from tscircuit/footprinter#929. The CLI converter and PCB rendering runtime now use the released package.

Stacked on #5370. The regression uses a pinned C82046 EasyEDA JSON fixture, checks diode identity and generated cathode polarity, and updates the same single PCB snapshot. Supplier availability and later catalog changes cannot affect the regression.

![C82046 diode-string PCB snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cli/0b94c3b5171bb0f6571a277f003498d1000d3715/tests/lib/import/__snapshots__/c82046-polarity-pcb.snap.svg)

Validation with the published dependency:
- `bun test tests/lib/import/c82046-polarity-repro.test.ts` — 3 passed; also passes with `fetch` blocked.
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` — passed.
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The existing end-to-end fixture test allows 60 seconds for discovery of its 624-pin i.MX6 case.

title: test: reproduce C82046 import losing diode identity and polarity
description: Reproduces a bug where the import of the C82046 component loses diode identity and polarity markings during the import process.
body:
Normal import of C82046 (onsemi MBR0530T1G) selects a generic `smdpads2` footprint string even though the supplier data identifies the part as a diode and pin 1 as its cathode. The resulting footprint has no diode identity or generated polarity markings.

Download C82046 live from EasyEDA in `beforeAll`, verify the cathode pin hints, and reproduce the missing diode family and explicit `_cathodepin1` modifier with `test.failing`. Network errors occur during setup, outside the expected-failure assertion. No raw EasyEDA JSON is checked in and production import behavior is unchanged.

Keep one PCB snapshot with fabrication notes enabled. The stacked solution updates that same snapshot to show Footprinter-generated diode markings. Preserving supplier artwork is not a requirement.

![C82046 repro PCB snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cli/ee7ed698490ffa4aebfa0ae5f039abf843c2618c/tests/lib/import/__snapshots__/c82046-polarity-pcb.snap.svg)

Validation:
- `bun test tests/lib/import/c82046-polarity-repro.test.ts` — 3 passed, including the expected failure.
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

title: Use existing JSCAD component model API
description: Generates procedural component models through the supported cadModel jscad  prop instead of the unsupported cadmodel jscad element. URL models continue to use the existing cadmodel and cadassembly paths. When one component contains both URL and JSCAD bodies, the URL representation takes precedence because the current component API accepts one CAD model value. This avoids synthetic components and preserves sourcePCB ownership. Regressions cover a single translucent JSCAD model, grouped multi-axis JSCAD geometry, and the mixed-model behavior.
body:
Generates procedural component models through the supported `cadModel={{ jscad }}` prop instead of the unsupported `<cadmodel jscad>` element. URL models continue to use the existing `<cadmodel>` and `<cadassembly>` paths.

When one component contains both URL and JSCAD bodies, the URL representation takes precedence because the current component API accepts one CAD model value. This avoids synthetic components and preserves source/PCB ownership. Regressions cover a single translucent JSCAD model, grouped multi-axis JSCAD geometry, and the mixed-model behavior.

title: fix: use native instance references for custom symbols (#640)
description: Fixes incorrect reference display for custom symbols in KiCad export, ensuring each instance shows its correct reference instead of duplicating the first instances reference.
body:
Custom symbols containing a `{REF}` label currently export the first component's resolved name into the shared library drawing, so U1 and U2 both display U1 while their correct Reference fields are hidden.

Recognize the resolved reference label by exact equality with its owning component's name, as described in #640. Remove that label from the shared drawing and display the placed symbol's native Reference field at the label's position, preserving its font size, alignment, and rotation. Both instances retain the same library ID. Updating an instance's reference updates the visible label.

This change is scoped to the whole-label reference case in #640. It changes only the converter; Circuit JSON and core are unchanged.

The seven updated generated-system SVG snapshots were visually reviewed. Repeated connector labels now read J1/J2/J3/J4 correctly; the remaining visible changes are the native Reference-field colour and alignment. No wiring, symbol geometry, or new label overlaps were found in those changes.

Stacked on #643, targeting `repro/issue-640-custom-symbol-reference`. Merge the repro first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

Fixes #640.

Validation:
- [Full CI after the snapshot update](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/actions/runs/38772844671): 207 tests passed, 0 failed; typecheck and format checks also passed.
- The latest shared font-size cleanup passes the two focused tests, typecheck, and formatting. Its generated KiCad output is unchanged across the four affected system fixtures; CI is rerunning for this commit.
- Both focused tests pass (31 assertions) using KiCad 10.0.1; both fail against the original exporter.
- Actual KiCad SVG output verifies U1/U2 each appear once, one library definition is shared, ordinary symbol text remains present, and changing U8 to U42 updates the visible reference.
- Field position, font size, alignment, and unchanged source text are asserted; generated PNG snapshots were visually inspected.
- Typecheck, build, and formatting of changed files pass.
- Related tests: 11 pass, 7 local snapshot failures. All seven also fail on the original exporter with identical image-diff percentages (`custom-symbol04`, `05`, `07`, `08`, `09`, `10`, and `repro15-custom-symbol-graphics-sch`). Those snapshots are unchanged.

![U1 and U2 using one shared symbol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/a9912e87594d2a063ab37195e82448aa8d9309fc/tests/sch/repros/__snapshots__/repro640-custom-symbol-reference.snap.png)

![Native reference placement and retained symbol text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/a9912e87594d2a063ab37195e82448aa8d9309fc/tests/sch/__snapshots__/custom-symbol11-reference-text.snap.png)

Adds a minimal TSX reproduction and a Circuit JSON/KiCad comparison PNG. Assertions capture the current incorrect library text and verify both rendered SVG labels are U1. This PR intentionally records the bug; the fix is stacked in #644.

title: fix: keep prefixed custom footprints in the project library
description: Fixes the export path for custom footprints with prefixed metadata names to ensure they are correctly classified in the project library.
body:
Custom footprints with metadata names such as `mylib:MyPart` were recorded under the full name but looked up as `MyPart`, causing library export to classify them as built-in. Store the bare metadata name so the footprint is exported to `footprints/mylib.pretty/MyPart.kicad_mod`.

Stacked on #645. This PR targets the reproduction branch and contains only the normalization change and the corrected snapshot path. Merge the reproduction first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

Validation:
- Changed the reproduction snapshot to the correct path and confirmed it failed before applying the fix; it passes afterward.
- The snapshot covers prefixed and unprefixed custom names, preserves the board's metadata name, and keeps the built-in resistor in `tscircuit_builtin.pretty`.
- Library suite: 13 passed initially; the model-download test passed on retry with network access. The remaining visual test has the same pre-existing 1.265% PNG mismatch on unchanged code (local threshold: 0.5%). Its snapshot was not changed.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run build` passed. Formatting reports only existing large-fixture warnings.

Fixes #639.

title: repro: snapshot prefixed custom footprint library placement
description: Fixes the export paths for custom footprints with prefixes, ensuring both prefixed and unprefixed versions are correctly exported and validated in the library.
body:
A custom footprint named `mylib:MyPart` is exported to `footprints/tscircuit_builtin.pretty/MyPart.kicad_mod`, while the same footprint named `MyPart` stays in `footprints/mylib.pretty/`. This reproduces #639 with a tscircuit-generated circuit and an inline snapshot of the exported footprint paths.

The test also checks that the board export preserves both metadata names and that a built-in resistor remains in the built-in library. The snapshot intentionally records the current bug; the fix is stacked in #647 and updates the affected path. Export-path text snapshots expose this issue directly because the footprint geometry is unchanged.

- `bun run typecheck` passed.
- `bun run format:check` passed (existing large-fixture warnings only).

Refs #639.

body:
Canvas currently ignores margins when `is_covered_with_solder_mask` is true and applies them when the flag is missing or false. This aligns pad and hole coverage with the unmodified published `circuit-to-svg@0.0.450` reference while preserving Canvas's existing colors and opaque board mask.

- Apply margins only with explicit coverage. Zero-margin SMT pads remain covered; non-plated and plated holes remain exposed.
- Match asymmetric openings and rounded corner expansion. Positive-margin substrate borders remain visible when board material is hidden.
- Enable `showSolderMask` in the existing SVG comparison helper and explicitly enable coverage in margin fixtures.
- Add 80 regression tests covering flag states, margins, layers, shapes, disabled masks, pour overlap, and preservation of the original palette/opacity. Comparison labels use the bundled stroke alphabet so Mac/Linux system fonts cannot change the snapshot.

The test reference is pinned to SVG 0.0.450, with the compatible circuit-json development dependency updated. No SVG patches or input rewriting are used. Canvas retains its correctly rotated positive pill-hole opening (the reference omits rotation), and its existing margin support for oval/polygon plated pads, which SVG does not yet support.

Validation: `bun test` (271 passed), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build` (ESM and DTS), and `bun run format:check` passed locally. Formatting reports only the existing oversized JSON fixture warning.

![Published circuit-to-svg versus circuit-to-canvas soldermask comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/cec3398e9a3f780ad6aabd812b308b65f25cff6f/tests/elements/__snapshots__/pcb-soldermask-svg-behavior.snap.png)

title: Add ti generate-sysconfig-url for hosted viewer links
description: Adds ti generate-sysconfig-url command to generate a URL for hosted read-only viewer links from a .syscfg file without requiring private viewer installation or TI tools.
body:
Adds `ti generate-sysconfig-url ./index.syscfg`, which prints a complete link for the hosted read-only viewer. It preserves the existing filename/source and supports `--viewer-url`; its default is https://sysconfig-viewer.vercel.app/.

The command uses the public `sysconfigts/url` codec, pinned to `e538c5dabfbb1f3d93830c7e3f7d0cc2ff2a5439` from https://github.com/tscircuit/sysconfigts/pull/3. The npm build bundles the encoder, so installed CLI users need no GitHub access, private viewer package, TI tools or SDK for URL generation. `generate-sysconfig-site` remains available separately. Automatic CLI/RunFrame tab wiring stays outside this change.

Rejects invalid input files, invalid UTF-8, oversized source and unsafe viewer addresses. Source is never executed or uploaded. Anyone with the complete URL can decode the source; encoding does not validate the target or pins.

Validation: 70 CLI tests, typecheck, formatting, npm build and the complete npm consumer check passed with the matching local codec contents. After replacing local development aliases with the actual public commit, focused URL tests and formatting pass. GitHub CI also passed formatting and the complete npm package check with the pinned public dependency, including clean installation and bundled CLI consumers. No temporary dependency aliases or private assets are committed.

Shared codec PR #3 is merged. This consumer now pins that merged main commit; its file tree is identical to the tested codec revision. No release or deployment is included.

title: Update SysConfig site setup to merged viewer PR #9
description: Updates the SysConfig site setup guide to reflect the merged viewer revision from PR 9, correcting installation instructions and clarifying user requirements for HTML regeneration.
body:
The SysConfig site setup guide still pins the viewer revision from PR #8. Update it to merged viewer main `ef3543c8f8098677afd821b2d335646d5f716285` from PR #9, including inline read-only settings, pin inspection, the two recorded I²C-owned GPIO dependencies and ownership-dependent Alternative Mux visibility.

The command already resolves the private viewer installed in the input project. Clarify that users must update that installation and regenerate existing HTML; updating TI alone does not replace it. Correct the description of the single form and recorded visibility cases. This changes only the guide, with no private viewer dependency or vendor UI assets added to the public TI package.

Validation: the actual `ti generate-sysconfig-site` entrypoint generated standalone pedometer HTML using a real viewer checkout whose tracked tree exactly matches the merged main revision (`867f918cc4b7bd074551e2967546b9707ffd719d`). Embedded source is byte-identical to the input and the resulting model displays eight GPIO entries. `git diff --check` passes. No local test suite or board build was rerun for this documentation-only update. The viewer's 92 tests and all three CI checks passed before merge.

TI PR #262 is already merged; this is its installation-guide follow-up. No deployment or merge is included.

title: Add shared SysConfig viewer URL encoding
description: Adds sysconfigtsurl so the public TI CLI can generate links without installing the private viewer, validating source size, filenames, Unicode, HTTP(S) viewer addresses, and bounded decompression.
body:
Adds `sysconfigts/url` so the public TI CLI can generate links without installing the private viewer. Both producers share the existing version 2 gzip/base64 format and preserve the filename and exact source.

Validates source size, filenames, Unicode, HTTP(S) viewer addresses and bounded decompression. The optional catalog is opaque transport data; the private viewer retains its own full catalog validation. This package contains no TI runtime, SDK or private viewer assets.

Validation: 44 tests (2 snapshots), typecheck and formatting pass. Parser exports remain unchanged. Consumer changes in TI and the private viewer will pin this revision.

title: Add native C firmware with PIO step generation
description: DRV8825 controllers currently generate STEP edges in MicroPython, so higher requested speeds can exceed the interpreters pulse throughput. Add a native Pico SDK C application that generates pulses in PIO and counts emitted edges with a separate PIO state machine and DMA. The application retains protocol 3, the existing dashboardgantry commands, 400 ms ramps, deferred GOTO starts, RGBUSB-PD controls, alarms, songs, and temperaturedriverheartbeatwatchdog protections. Native settings use two reserved flash sectors with checksum and partial-write recovery. A build fingerprint identifies the image on live boards. The legacy DRV8847 MicroPython implementation remains available; this native image targets the DRV8825RGB PCB. Validation: Cross-built the UF2 with Pico SDK 2.3.1; native motion, protocolprotection, and settings tests passed with UBSan. Existing 45 Python tests and dashboard, song, single-motor, gantry, and saved-position checks passed. Flashed both physical controllers and checked their build fingerprints. Driver-disabled electrical tests emitted exact requested counts at 1k, 64k, 128k, and 200k physical pulsessec with zero PIO queue underruns. At the 200k setting, observed throughput was approximately 199.7k pulsessec on both boards. Verified heartbeat expiry and USB disconnect stop pulse generation, heartbeats do not resume it, settings survive restart, and restarts return to disabled 5 V with fresh position sessions. No shaft movement or loaded mechanical performance was tested. Independent pulse-widthjitter measurement, loaded torque, and physical positional accuracy remain unverified. CI adds host native tests and an ARM UF2 build.
body:
DRV8825 controllers currently generate STEP edges in MicroPython, so higher requested speeds can exceed the interpreter's pulse throughput. Add a native Pico SDK C application that generates pulses in PIO and counts emitted edges with a separate PIO state machine and DMA.

The application retains protocol 3, the existing dashboard/gantry commands, 400 ms ramps, deferred GOTO starts, RGB/USB-PD controls, alarms, songs, and temperature/driver/heartbeat/watchdog protections. Native settings use two reserved flash sectors with checksum and partial-write recovery. A build fingerprint identifies the image on live boards. The legacy DRV8847 MicroPython implementation remains available; this native image targets the DRV8825/RGB PCB.

Validation:
- Cross-built the UF2 with Pico SDK 2.3.1; native motion, protocol/protection, and settings tests passed with UBSan.
- Existing 45 Python tests and dashboard, song, single-motor, gantry, and saved-position checks passed.
- Flashed both physical controllers and checked their build fingerprints. Driver-disabled electrical tests emitted exact requested counts at 1k, 64k, 128k, and 200k physical pulses/sec with zero PIO queue underruns. At the 200k setting, observed throughput was approximately 199.7k pulses/sec on both boards.
- Verified heartbeat expiry and USB disconnect stop pulse generation, heartbeats do not resume it, settings survive restart, and restarts return to disabled 5 V with fresh position sessions.

No shaft movement or loaded mechanical performance was tested. Independent pulse-width/jitter measurement, loaded torque, and physical positional accuracy remain unverified. CI adds host native tests and an ARM UF2 build.

title: Add macOS terminal installation without browser quarantine
description: Add a macOS terminal installer that downloads a specified release with curl, selects arm64 or x64 automatically, verifies the selected archive against SHA256SUMS before extracting, and preserves all redistribution notices.
body:
Browser-downloaded macOS releases inherit quarantine metadata from the browser and can be blocked by Gatekeeper despite having a valid ad hoc signature. The metadata is added on the user's Mac, so removing attributes during release packaging cannot prevent this behavior.

Add a macOS terminal installer that downloads a specified release with curl, selects arm64 or x64 automatically, verifies the selected archive against SHA256SUMS before extracting, and preserves all redistribution notices. Existing destinations are refused, and temporary downloads are cleaned up. This provides an installation path that does not acquire browser quarantine and requires no Apple account, sudo, or Bun/Node installation.

Document the installer in the README and include a source-commit-pinned command in daily/manual release notes. Document the file-specific quarantine workaround for existing browser downloads. Browser downloads remain subject to Gatekeeper; this change does not claim to make them notarized or disable macOS security settings.

Validation:
- `bun test tests/install-macos.test.ts tests/daily-release.test.ts` — 26 passed, including both architectures, checksum rejection, download failures, and preservation of existing installations.
- `sh -n scripts/install-macos.sh` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Installed the published `daily-2026-10-15` arm64 release on macOS with the new installer: checksum passed, no `com.apple.quarantine` on the executable, signature verification passed, and `tsci --version` returned `0.0.2895`. The version check ran outside the sandbox because startup opens a loopback asset server.

title: Embed the eval worker in the standalone RunFrame bundle
description: Embed the CLIs eval worker through RunFrames existing INJECT_TSCIRCUIT_EVAL_WEB_WORKER_BLOB_URL placeholder during binary compilation, allowing the browser to start the embedded code from a Blob URL without a separate worker file or endpoint.
body:
Embed the CLI's eval worker through RunFrame's existing `INJECT_TSCIRCUIT_EVAL_WEB_WORKER_BLOB_URL` placeholder during binary compilation. The browser starts the embedded code from a Blob URL, without a separate worker file or endpoint.

Pin [CLI #5384](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5384) to reuse the existing eval version global and avoid online startup discovery. No new dependencies or RunFrame changes are needed.

Validated worker byte preservation, JS CDN tests, type checking, native binary compilation, and existing binary smoke tests. AT8548 and RP2040 rendered with external networking blocked and no CDN worker or version-discovery requests.

The existing smoke test copies the compiled executable into the project, waits for initial file synchronization, and checks that the executable was excluded. Type checking and the compiled build/dev/browser smoke pass on macOS ARM64.

The 50 native `<copperpour />` elements use tscircuit's default 0.2 mm clearance, thermal reliefs, and solder mask coverage. All routing layers remain available to the normal autorouter.

title: Enable default autorouting and KiCad copper pours for all 25 boards
description: Board sources previously disabled routing by default and most lacked copper-pour declarations. Enable the normal autorouter on all 25 boards with routeRemainingtrue and add 1,147 native pour regions from the pinned KiCad zones, preserving their nets, layers, priorities, and board boundaries. Component placement, footprints, electrical net definitions, and schematics are unchanged. Board sources previously disabled routing by default and most lacked copper-pour declarations. Enable the normal autorouter on all 25 boards with `routeRemaining={true}` and add 1,147 native pour regions from the pinned KiCad zones, preserving their nets, layers, priorities, and board boundaries. Existing board definitions also match byte-for-byte after excluding routing flags and added pour declarations. GitHub CI passed and generated inspection HTML.

title: fix: honor length units in diode pad geometry
description: Fixes incorrect pitch and pad dimensions in diode pad geometry generation by properly parsing length units.
body:
`sod123w_p100mil` currently generates a 100 mm pitch instead of 2.54 mm because `Number.parseFloat` ignores the unit suffix. Pad length and width have the same problem in the affected generators.

Use the existing `length.parse` conversion for pitch (`p` or `pad_spacing`), pad length (`pl`), and pad width (`pw`) across 19 SOD, SMA/SMB/SMC/SMF, and MELF generators.

These existing footprint strings already handle mils correctly:

| Working reference | Footprint string | Existing result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [SOD-123F pad generator](https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/blob/3065398619c4811553cceef32c19d59641b28acb/src/fn/sod123f.ts#L103-L105) | `sod123f_p100mil` | 2.54 mm pitch |
| [Pin row length fields](https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/blob/3065398619c4811553cceef32c19d59641b28acb/src/fn/pinrow.ts#L49-L52) | `pinrow2_p100mil` | 2.54 mm pitch |
| [SMD pad length fields](https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/blob/3065398619c4811553cceef32c19d59641b28acb/src/fn/smdpads.ts#L15-L17) | `smdpads2_p100mil_pw40mil_ph30mil` | 2.54 mm pitch; 1.016 × 0.762 mm pads |
| [DIP mil conversion](https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/blob/3065398619c4811553cceef32c19d59641b28acb/src/fn/dip.ts#L18-L21) | `dip8_w300mil_p100mil` | 7.62 mm row spacing; 2.54 mm pitch |

Regressions use each package's established default dimensions expressed in mils, inches, millimeters, and unitless values, with `sod123f` as a working control. Numeric assertions check pad positions, sizes, and pin identities, while visual checks reuse the existing package SVG snapshots.

Only one new SVG is added: the public `sod123w` string case uses its established 2.8 mm pitch and 1.2 mm square pads, expressed in mils, with fabrication notes visible.

Validation:
- `bun test tests/diode-length-units.test.ts` — 21 passed.
- `bun test` — 639 passed, 0 failed.
- `bun run build` — JavaScript and declarations passed for the unchanged production implementation.
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Rendered and visually inspected the new SOD-123W snapshot.

Related: #887 covers the SOD subset of this fix. This PR also covers the affected SMA/SMB/SMC/SMF and MELF generators.

title: fix: parse explicit polarity pins in LED footprint strings
description: Fixes parsing of explicit polarity pins in LED footprint strings to prevent errors related to diode pin assignments.
body:
LED footprint strings such as `led0603_cathodepin1` throw `Diode cathode pin must be 1 or 2`, while the equivalent numeric builder works. Normalize `anodepin` and `cathodepin` through the existing base schema before creating fabrication notes, matching the diode fix in #929.

Regression tests cover standard and custom LED footprints, both polarity modifiers on either pin, conflicting assignments, and two SVG snapshots with fabrication notes visible.

- Changed source/test files pass Biome formatting; `git diff --check` passed.
- Visually inspected both new SVG snapshots.

Related: #926 also includes LED polarity normalization as part of its broader silkscreen changes.

title: Generate internallyConnectedPins in EasyEDA component TSX
description: Adds a typed internallyConnectedPins option to convertRawEasyToTsx, convertBetterEasyToTsx, and generateTypescriptComponent, allowing for better handling of internally connected pins in EasyEDA components.
body:
Component TSX generation belongs in the converter rather than a CLI AST postprocessor. Add a typed `internallyConnectedPins` option to `convertRawEasyToTsx`, `convertBetterEasyToTsx`, and `generateTypescriptComponent`, alongside the existing `pinAttributes` option. Chip, pushbutton, switch, and connector templates emit the groups before the caller's props spread; omission preserves existing output and an explicit empty array remains an override.

The CLI continues to fetch/validate datasheet metadata and passes the groups into conversion. No registry requests or API source evaluation are introduced in the converter.

Tests use the original TS-1187A-B-A-B/C318884 fixture and cover both conversion entrypoints, all supported component templates, mixed string/numeric identifiers, empty groups, caller overrides, valid TSX syntax, unchanged existing props, and immutable inputs. Build and typecheck pass locally, along with the new regression and existing pin-attribute tests.

Adds a PR preview package workflow following the existing core repository pattern so downstream CLI PR https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5397 can consume a reviewed converter build before the next npm release. The CLI PR removes its `add-internally-connected-pins-to-tsx.ts` helper.

title: repro: female pinheader renders male CAD with explicit footprint
description: Fixes rendering issue where a female pinheader with an explicit footprint incorrectly renders male pins instead of female sockets in 3D.
body:
`<pinheader gender="female" footprint="pinrow4" pinCount={4} />` renders male pins in 3D, even though its source component retains `gender: "female"`. The same female header without an explicit footprint renders sockets correctly. Both should select a female CAD model.

This reproduction compares those two inputs on one labeled board and preserves the current mismatch in a 3D snapshot. An expected-failing assertion checks that the explicit header's CAD footprint contains `_female`; running it as a normal test fails with `Received: "pinrow4"`. There are no implementation or dependency changes.

![J1 uses an explicit pinrow4 footprint and renders male pins; J2 uses an automatic footprint and renders female sockets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/core/fd09fc364e35cf7f92df0258b167049f9c120f29/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-female-pinheader-explicit-footprint-simple-3d.snap.png)

The earlier fix in #2330 appends `_female` to implied footprints. An explicit footprint takes precedence in `resolveFootprint()`, so that suffix is never applied in this case.

Validation:

- Ran the repro without `test.failing`: it fails at the desired CAD assertion, after the source-gender checks, automatic-header control, and snapshot comparison succeed.
- Ran the committed repro and `pin-header-female-cad-model.test.tsx` without snapshot updates: 2 pass, 0 fail, including the expected failure.
- Inspected the labeled 3D snapshot. Biome formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full type check passes: `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 bunx tsc --noEmit`.

title: Preserve required schematic branches when removing redundant net-label wires
description: Preserves required schematic branches and routes when removing redundant net-label wires, ensuring connectivity to fixed net labels without altering source-net connectivity.
body:
Core removes whole solver traces when their endpoint pins already have fixed net labels. Solver paths can terminate on the middle of another path, so that test can remove a shared rail while leaving a dependent branch dangling. In the PD sheet from #4648, the EP branch continues through the GND symbol after its shared rail is removed.

Replace that pin-ID filter with connectivity-aware handling of the emitted wire geometry in core. Split same-net routes at their actual contacts with each other and with the existing label wires, then retain the segments needed to connect terminals to those labels. Preserve existing wires, required shared rails, and routes with no path to a fixed label. This selects among existing segments; it does not reroute or change source-net connectivity.

Use the published solver's normalized terminal coordinates as well as core's real-pin stubs, so projected custom-symbol pins remain connected. Preserve routes that carry inline labels by the placement's exact trace ID. Compute crossings over the retained routes and existing label wires within the current sheet, retaining trace metadata for database updates.

The solver API and dependency are unchanged. `package.json` keeps the existing jscdn URL at version `0.0.230`. The PD sheet fixture itself is unchanged.

Regression coverage includes:

- The complete PD sheet: all three bottom ground pins reach the fixed GND label, with no wire through the symbol.
- Branches that require part of a shared rail, required continuations beyond a label, other nets, and disconnected routes.
- Projected custom-symbol terminals in all four directions. Snapshot captions explain the intentionally inset red pin stem and the expected green wire at the symbol boundary.
- Inline-label carrier wires. The snapshot identifies R3's inline SIGNAL annotation and the wire it must retain.

Validation:

- The PD regression fails on the unchanged repro branch. The projected-terminal and inline-label regressions fail with the earlier implementation; all pass with this change.
- Seven focused regression tests pass, including the full PD sheet and existing crossing repro131.
- Typecheck, package build, distribution smoke tests, and formatting pass.
- Reviewed the updated schematic snapshots.
- Full CI passes at `97b247ffe`: 1,929 tests passed, 51 skipped, 0 failed across all 10 shards. Typecheck, formatting, package preview, and distribution smoke checks also pass.

Stacked on repro PR #4648.

title: Use imported internal pin connections in core checks
description: Supplier Circuit JSON can contain permanent internal pin groups, but core discards those groups while importing the footprint. Retain the groups as derived component metadata, resolve supplier-local source-port IDs to component pin names, and use them for emitted source connectivity and missing-trace checks. Explicit internallyConnectedPins, including , takes precedence without mutating user props or imported Circuit JSON. Groundpower connection queries now follow permanent internal contacts on both ends of a trace; overlapping groups are traversed transitively. Ground attributes and aliases take precedence over fallback power-name detection, so a ground ball address such as V3 does not disable automatic decoupling trace limits when reached through an internal group. Push buttons opt into parts-engine datasheet enrichment so a four-terminal switch can share AB and CD without connecting its momentary switch terminals. Runtime datasheet enrichment requires the parts-engine change in https:github.comtscircuitparts-enginepull68 to be published and used by the calling parts engine. This PR consumes the existing Circuit JSON internal-connection field and needs no schema change. Source design-rule checks also compare the explicit internallyConnectedPins prop against datasheet groups and warn when a reported connection is missing from the declaration. For example: The datasheet reports pins A and B are internally connected, but the internallyConnectedPins prop isnt set on SW1. Imported defaults do not suppress this warning. Empty or incomplete declarations warn too; pin aliases, numbers, and transitive groups count as equivalent declarations. Warnings update or disappear when the declaration changes, and respect the DRC disable controls. Custom-footprint chips, pushbuttons, and op amps can fetch comparison metadata even without pinAttributes; supplier-footprint imports reuse their existing metadata request. Fetching comparison facts does not replace custom geometry or mutate props. Validation: 25 focused tests pass, including suppliercustom footprint warnings, missing and empty declarations, equivalent aliasestransitive groups, disabled checks, warning updates, imported connectivity, and existing datasheet pin-attribute checks. Labeled PCB snapshots are included and visually reviewed. Package build, typecheck, and formatting pass. Homepage smoke test: rebuilt the exact homepage releases of seveibarnrf-smart-watch0.1.1, imrishabh18rp2040-motor-controller1.0.41, absewifi-smart-switch1.0.29, and absegameboy1.0.15 against the PR and its base, using the same cached live network responses and the parts-engine internal-pin support. All 274 components rendered with identical diagnostics after the routing-disable fix. This check keeps autorouting disabled. Async datasheet validation now respects routing-disable controls on update, preventing routing diagnostics during a disabled-routing render. A regression test covers both platform and board controls. seveibarf1c100s-linux-dev-board1.9.2 fails on both versions before rendering: its routingBoundaryRef callback calls the absent internal method doInitialPcbImplicitCopperPourRender. This existing compatibility issue prevents a complete smoke test of that board.
body:
Supplier Circuit JSON can contain permanent internal pin groups, but core discards those groups while importing the footprint. Retain the groups as derived component metadata, resolve supplier-local source-port IDs to component pin names, and use them for emitted source connectivity and missing-trace checks. Explicit `internallyConnectedPins`, including `[]`, takes precedence without mutating user props or imported Circuit JSON.

Ground/power connection queries now follow permanent internal contacts on both ends of a trace; overlapping groups are traversed transitively. Ground attributes and aliases take precedence over fallback power-name detection, so a ground ball address such as `V3` does not disable automatic decoupling trace limits when reached through an internal group. Push buttons opt into parts-engine datasheet enrichment so a four-terminal switch can share A–B and C–D without connecting its momentary switch terminals.

Runtime datasheet enrichment requires the parts-engine change in https://github.com/tscircuit/parts-engine/pull/68 to be published and used by the calling parts engine. This PR consumes the existing Circuit JSON internal-connection field and needs no schema change.

Source design-rule checks also compare the explicit `internallyConnectedPins` prop against datasheet groups and warn when a reported connection is missing from the declaration. For example: “The datasheet reports pins A and B are internally connected, but the internallyConnectedPins prop isn't set on SW1.” Imported defaults do not suppress this warning. Empty or incomplete declarations warn too; pin aliases, numbers, and transitive groups count as equivalent declarations. Warnings update or disappear when the declaration changes, and respect the DRC disable controls.

Custom-footprint chips, pushbuttons, and op amps can fetch comparison metadata even without `pinAttributes`; supplier-footprint imports reuse their existing metadata request. Fetching comparison facts does not replace custom geometry or mutate props.

Validation: 25 focused tests pass, including supplier/custom footprint warnings, missing and empty declarations, equivalent aliases/transitive groups, disabled checks, warning updates, imported connectivity, and existing datasheet pin-attribute checks. Labeled PCB snapshots are included and visually reviewed. Package build, typecheck, and formatting pass.


Related PRs: website https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/pull/5454; core https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4667; CLI https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5397; parts engine https://github.com/tscircuit/parts-engine/pull/68.

Homepage smoke test: rebuilt the exact homepage releases of `seveibar/nrf-smart-watch@0.1.1`, `imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller@1.0.41`, `abse/wifi-smart-switch@1.0.29`, and `abse/gameboy@1.0.15` against the PR and its base, using the same cached live network responses and the parts-engine internal-pin support. All 274 components rendered with identical diagnostics after the routing-disable fix. This check keeps autorouting disabled. Async datasheet validation now respects routing-disable controls on update, preventing routing diagnostics during a disabled-routing render. A regression test covers both platform and board controls.

`seveibar/f1c100s-linux-dev-board@1.9.2` fails on both versions before rendering: its `routingBoundaryRef` callback calls the absent internal method `doInitialPcbImplicitCopperPourRender`. This existing compatibility issue prevents a complete smoke test of that board.

title: Preserve native keepout outlines with verified autorouter coverage (foolow-up to #4597)
description: Preserves native keepout outlines and improves autorouter coverage by implementing an approved patch from a previous pull request, ensuring no uncovered stroke points and reducing obstacles significantly.
body:
This is a follow-up to [#4597](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4597), whose fix was already [reviewed and approved by Seve (seveibar)](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4597#pullrequestreview-5541141104).
The original PR merged into the upstream repro branch, while [#4602](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4602) brought only the fork’s baseline reproductions into main, leaving the approved fix out of main.
This PR carries that same approved patch directly to **main**, with no additional implementation changes.

Sample024’s five open keepout arcs currently expand into 1,430 SRJ obstacles and leave sampled stroke points uncovered; native rotated rectangles and square joins/caps reduce this to 475 obstacles with zero uncovered samples while preserving the openings and layers.
The published `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter@^0.0.985`, containing [autorouter #3098](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3098), preserves coverage when preprocessing these rotated rectangles for [dataset-srj24 #14](https://github.com/tscircuit/dataset-srj24/pull/14).

Validation:
- All three existing reproduction tests pass: 286 → 95 obstacles per arc, 590 → 0 uncovered stroke samples per arc, and 2 → 0 uncovered samples for the thin 45° keepout.
- The cherry-picked patch produces an identical source tree to the approved fix; diff whitespace check passes.

All three repro tests and baseline snapshots already exist on main. This PR modifies them to assert and show the corrected results.

title: fix: default polygon-pad drill offsets to zero
description: Fixes rendering issue by defaulting omitted polygon-pad drill offsets to zero, preventing NaN coordinates and misplaced holes.
body:
Circuit JSON allows drill offsets to be omitted, defaulting to zero. The polygon-pad renderer assumes both offsets are present, so rendering unparsed input produces `NaN` coordinates and misplaced or missing holes. This change applies the same zero defaults used by other plated-hole shapes while preserving explicitly supplied offsets.

The issue is visible in the comparison snapshot from [circuit-json-webgpu PR #41](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/pull/41). On the left, the pinned `circuit-to-svg` renderer places the pink drill at the top-left edge instead of inside the red polygon pad. On the right, WebGPU renders the drill at the correct pad centre.

![Polygon-pad comparison: misplaced drill in circuit-to-svg on the left, centred drill in WebGPU on the right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rushabhcodes/circuit-json-webgpu/e6cc172867338ec8ab3879d7324e88551ff9108c/tests/snapshots/features/pcb-plated-hole-polygon-4b65385a5db9.png)

Add a visual regression covering circular, oval, pill, and rotated-pill drills with both offsets omitted or only one supplied. The raw-input SVG must match the schema-normalized SVG. The regression fails with `NaN` on the original code and passes after the two-line fix; existing explicit-offset snapshots remain unchanged.

Validation: all four targeted plated-hole tests pass; the new SVG snapshot was rendered, visually inspected, and verified without snapshot updates. Type checking, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.

title: Check actual footprint geometry against board boundaries
description: Fixes incorrect reporting of component overhangs by using actual footprint geometry for boundary checks instead of bounding rectangles.
body:
Fixes https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/4635

The outside-board check used component bounding rectangles except for a single circular plated hole. Adding a courtyard disabled that exception and incorrectly reported a 0.48 mm overhang in the rounded board corner.

Use the existing Circuit JSON-to-FlattenJS converter to check actual pad, hole, and courtyard outlines. This handles offset circles, multiple pads, and other supported shapes through the same geometry path, and removes the circular mounting-pad helper. Retain the component rectangle when its bounds are not explained by the physical footprint, preserving separately sized bodies and components without footprint geometry. Containment uses the actual polygons; diagnostic overhang distances use circular geometry or boundary samples rather than invented rectangle corners.

One regression test matches the emitted Circuit JSON, accepts the original and offset courtyard, and matches the error geometry when the courtyard genuinely extends off-board. Confirmed that the offset case fails against the earlier special-case patch.

Validation: `bun test` (663 passed), `bun run build`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, Biome formatting, and `git diff --check`.

title: Preserve filled fabrication polarity artwork on a real LED board
description: Fixes the issue where filled fabrication symbols for polarity markings on a real LED board were not exported correctly in Gerber files, ensuring they are preserved during the fabrication export process.
body:
Stack: **#202 (reproduction, merge first) → #197 (fix)**. This PR targets the reproduction branch.

A real LCSC C41413180 / XINGLIGHT XL-1615RGBC-WS2812B-S LED has four filled fabrication symbols, including its + and − markings. The old exporter treats them as zero-width strokes, so they disappear from fabrication Gerbers.

The reproduction uses the complete imported four-pad footprint on a routed VDD/GND/DIN/DOUT breakout board, retaining real supplier silkscreen and artwork. [#202's board snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/blob/codex/repro-real-led-fabrication-board/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/real-led-fabrication-board.snap.svg) shows the symbols present in the input and missing in the export. [This PR's corrected board snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/blob/codex/fix-filled-fabrication-polarity-paths/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/real-led-fabrication-board.snap.svg) shows the same artwork restored alongside the real lands, traces, board outline and reference labels.

The comparison explicitly overlays the fabrication layer with copper/silk for inspection; these are fabrication symbols, not newly added printed silkscreen or a claim about JLCPCB's layer handling.

Emits closed Gerber regions for filled fabrication paths, independently respects `has_stroke`, and avoids zero-diameter apertures for fill-only artwork. The board assertion changes from the reproduced zero regions to four preserved regions. Focused tests also cover top/bottom layers, Y-axis flipping and fill/stroke combinations. Standalone detail snapshots remain 800 px wide; the full board comparison is 1604 × 748 px.

Validation: **197 tests pass**, production build and changed-file format checks pass. Reproduction #202 passes 193 tests without exporter changes. No new documentation files.

- `bun run build`

description: Corrects the crystal propertys documentation example from an invalid 2pin to the valid two_pin value for the pinVariant property.
body:
The crystal property's table recommends `pinVariant="2pin"`, but that value is rejected by `CrystalProps`. Change the example to `"two_pin"`, the supported two-terminal variant, so readers can copy a valid value into their circuit.

### What was wrong

[Current crystal documentation page](https://docs.tscircuit.com/elements/crystal#properties).

The actual `PinVariant` type and runtime schema accept **`"two_pin"` or `"four_pin"`**. The table's `"2pin"` example fails validation with:

```text
Invalid enum value. Expected 'two_pin' | 'four_pin', received '2pin'
```

### Before and after

| Property | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pinVariant` example | `"2pin"` — rejected by the schema | `"two_pin"` — accepted by the schema |

| Before: current docs page | After: corrected docs page |
| --- | --- |
| ![Current crystal property table recommends the invalid 2pin value](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/docs/916ac5f8e6176e7bbf1d4d3fda443e23fb617a52/review-screenshots/crystal-before.png) | ![Corrected crystal property table recommends the supported two_pin value](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/docs/916ac5f8e6176e7bbf1d4d3fda443e23fb617a52/review-screenshots/crystal-after.png) |

Before is the live docs page; after is the locally built production page. The correction is one example value in `docs/elements/crystal.mdx`; the runnable circuit already uses the default two-pin crystal. Screenshots are hosted separately from the PR diff.

### Validation and preview

- Checked the real `crystalProps` runtime schema: `2pin` fails; `two_pin` and `four_pin` pass.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run build` passed.
- Opened the built `/elements/crystal` page in Chromium and verified the corrected property row.
- **[Review the fixed documentation page](https://docs-git-fork-devesh36-fix-crystal-pin-variant-docs-tscircuit.vercel.app/elements/crystal#properties)** — verified HTTP 200 and the corrected `two_pin` property row.

title: fix: honour pcb_plated_hole drill offset and route every variant
description: Fixes the emission of plated holes by correctly applying drill offsets and routing all variants, addressing a bug where offsets were ignored and some variants emitted nothing.
body:
## Summary

`pcb_plated_hole` carries `hole_offset_x` and `hole_offset_y`, which give the
drill position relative to the pad centre. They were never read anywhere in the
package, so every plated hole drill was emitted on the pad centre.

On a `pmp23595` board in the circuit json dataset, four holes are offset by
2.286 mm in y. All four were emitted on the pad centre instead, a 2.286 mm
error on each, on the only plated holes in that dataset with a nonzero offset.

While localizing this I found a second defect in the same dispatch: a plated
hole with `shape: "oval"` matched no branch and emitted no hole at all. Both are
fixed here.

## The bug

`pcb_plated_hole` had no dedicated emission path. It was collected into the
same `holes` array as `pcb_hole` and dispatched on `hole_shape ?? shape`, and
the drill position was read straight off the pad centre:

```ts
const holeX = getHoleCoordinate(hole.x)
const holeY = getHoleCoordinate(hole.y)
```

`grep -rn "hole_offset_x" lib/` returned nothing. `lib/pill-geometry.ts` had the
same gap, reading `hole.x` and `hole.y` directly in `getPillGeometry`.

## The dispatch gap

The existing dispatch handled `circle`, `pill` and `rotated_pill`. Two of the
six `pcb_plated_hole` variants therefore emitted nothing:

| variant | routed before | routed after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PcbPlatedHoleCircle` | circle | circle |
| `PcbHoleCircularWithRectPad` | circle, via `hole_shape` | unchanged |
| `PcbHolePillWithRectPad` | pill, via `hole_shape` | unchanged |
| `PcbHoleRotatedPillWithRectPad` | rotated pill, via `hole_shape` | unchanged |
| `PcbHoleWithPolygonPad` | via `hole_shape` | unchanged |
| `PcbPlatedHoleOval` (`shape: "oval"`) | **nothing emitted** | pill |

The oval variant is now routed to the pill emitter. That branch is gated on
`hole.type === "pcb_plated_hole"`, because the non-plated `pcb_hole` also has an
oval variant that falls through today, and routing that too would change
`pcb_hole` output. That separate gap is left alone on purpose.

## Offset semantics

The offset is added directly to the pad centre in board coordinates and is not
rotated by any pad or hole rotation. This matches `circuit-json-to-gltf`, which
this package already depends on:

```js
const relX = plated.x - boardCenter.x + holeOffsetX
```

Two variants name the drill rotation differently. `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad`
uses `hole_ccw_rotation`; the oval and polygon pad variants use `ccw_rotation`.
The pill emitter now reads `hole_ccw_rotation ?? ccw_rotation ?? 0`.

## Tests

Two fixtures, deliberately covering different things.

`plated-hole-offset-real.json`, from the real board. 3.0 KB, the
`pcb_board` plus the four offset holes, with none of the 498 pads, 944 traces or
735 vias. Expectations are derived from each record's own `x`, `y` and offset
fields rather than a hardcoded table. This fixture also pins the *shape* of the
production case: the offset is on one axis only, with the other axis holding
float noise around `1e-16`. A diagonal synthetic offset would not catch a
regression that mishandles one axis.

**`plated-hole-variants.json`, all six schema variants.** This exists because
real data cannot cover the matrix. Across the whole circuit json dataset:

| variant | holes | nonzero offset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `circle` | 505 | 0 |
| `pill` | 142 | 0 |
| `circular_hole_with_rect_pad` | 82 | 4 |
| `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad` | 10 | 0 |
| `hole_with_polygon_pad` | 3 | 0 |
| `pill_hole_with_rect_pad` | **0** | 0 |

`pill_hole_with_rect_pad` has no instance anywhere, and real producers emit
`"pill"` rather than `"oval"`, so the new oval branch is never exercised by
production data either. The synthetic fixture uses a diagonal `(0.5, 0.3)` so
both axes are covered, and asserts the absence of offset fields on the two
variants that have none in the schema.

Both fixtures include the pad fields the schema requires, but no pad geometry is
emitted.

Both tests were confirmed to fail against the previous code:

- real test: `emittedAtExpectedOffset: false`, `emittedAtPadCentreInstead: true`
- synthetic: 4 of 5 tests fail, with `PcbPlatedHoleOval` reporting
  `hasCircle: false`, that is, emitting nothing

Suite: 37 pass, 0 fail. `tsc` clean, `format:check` clean.

## One note on method

The synthetic test asserts position by translation invariance rather than by
reading coordinates back out of the STEP text. A pill never emits a point at its
own centre, and a single `CIRCLE` edge exposes no centre point either, so a
literal coordinate check does not work across all shapes. A variant emitted at
pad centre plus offset must produce byte-identical output to the same variant
moved to that point with no offset set, which does. A direct cylinder-axis
coordinate assertion is included alongside it for the circular variants, and the
real-data test uses literal coordinates throughout.

title: fix: avoid hierarchical schematic filename collisions
description: Fixes filename collisions in hierarchical schematics by reserving the root filename and renaming child filenames accordingly to prevent overwriting.
body:
## Motivation

`getOutputFiles({ schematicFilename: "index.kicad_sch" })` can return two files named `index.kicad_sch` when a child schematic sheet is also named `index`. Directory and ZIP exporters then overwrite the root schematic with the child sheet.

## Changes

- reserve the normalized root filename while allocating hierarchical child filenames
- rebuild already-generated hierarchical files when the requested root filename requires a child rename, keeping the root `Sheetfile` references consistent
- cover a root/child collision together with slash and space sanitization

## Validation

- the new regression fails on `main` with duplicate `index.kicad_sch` filenames

title: fix: give library-symbol instances with different pin numbering their own lib ids
description: Fixes the issue where multiple instances of the same library symbol with different pin numbering share a single lib id, causing incorrect symbol resolution in KiCad.
body:
Fixes the case #581 leaves open from #579: two instances of one library symbol that need different pin numbering.

Since #581 (released in 0.0.223), each instance's pins are numbered from its own circuit ports. Instances of one library symbol still share one lib id, though. When two instances need different numbering, the export writes two `(symbol "Device:led_right" …)` definitions under that one lib id. KiCad resolves both instances through a single definition, so one part comes out reversed with no warning.

Repro on current main (`2b33613`, released as 0.0.234) with tscircuit 0.0.2905 and `kicad-cli` 10.0.1 from `ghcr.io/kicad/kicad:10.0.1`:

```tsx
<board width="20mm" height="20mm">
  <led name="D1" color="red" footprint="0603" pcbX={-3} />
  <led name="D2" color="red" footprint="0603" pcbX={3}
       pinLabels={{ pin1: ["cathode", "K"], pin2: ["anode", "A"] }} />
  <resistor name="R1" resistance="1k" footprint="0402" pcbX={-3} pcbY={5} />
  <resistor name="R2" resistance="1k" footprint="0402" pcbX={3} pcbY={5} />
  <trace from=".D1 > .pin1" to=".R1 > .pin1" />
  <trace from=".D2 > .pin1" to=".R2 > .pin1" />
</board>
```

`kicad-cli sch export netlist --format kicadxml`:

```
main:     Net-(D1-1)    D1 pin 2, R1 pin 1   <- the source says D1.pin1 -> R1.pin1
          Net-(D2-2)    D2 pin 1, R2 pin 1
this PR:  Net-(D1-Pad1) D1 pin 1, R1 pin 1
          Net-(D2-2)    D2 pin 1, R2 pin 1
```

ERC is unchanged: the same 16 violations (off-grid endpoints, the `Device` library not configured, and the intentionally open pins) on main and on this branch.

What changes:
- `AddLibrarySymbolsStage` records the pin numbering each lib id has been emitted with. An instance whose numbering differs from the first one gets its own lib id (`Device:led_right_2`, and so on), and `AddSchematicSymbolsStage` places it with that id. Instances that agree keep sharing the original id, so existing exports don't change. No existing snapshot changes.
- `tests/sch/repros/repro579-shared-library-symbol-pin-numbers.test.tsx` places three LEDs and draws D2 the other way round, using the same port swap as the last test in `repro579-library-symbol-pin-numbers.test.tsx`. It checks that D2 gets its own lib id with the reversed numbering, and that D3 still shares D1's. It fails on main and passes here.

This PR first carried its own pin-matching rule for #579. #581 replaced that, so the branch is now rebased onto main and cut down to the shared lib-id case. An earlier version of this PR threw on this conflict. This version exports the design correctly instead.

Validation: I ran the full suite inside `ghcr.io/kicad/kicad:10.0.1` (the `test` job's image) on main and on this branch, after `download-references` and `download-demos`. The branch adds no failure that main doesn't also have. The only failures locally are PNG raster snapshots, which don't rasterise the same outside CI, and tests that need network access. All the schematic SVG snapshots pass, including repro21, repro22 and repro23. `bunx tsc --noEmit` is clean and `biome format` is applied.

title: feat: detect separated high-pass RC filter components
description: Detects and reports separated high-pass RC filter components in schematic analysis, ensuring proper grouping for readability.
body:
The headphone output draws C43–R25 and C44–R26 apart, so each series capacitor and its grounded resistor are difficult to read as one branch. `HighPassRcFilterPlacementSolver` reports `HighPassRcFilterComponentsNotGrouped` for both pairs. The existing `SeriesRcFilterPlacementSolver` covers the opposite topology: a series resistor followed by a grounded capacitor.

Stack: **#293 (TSX repro) → this PR (analyzer and correction)**. Merge the repro first.

## Before and after

![Complete headphone block, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8919d4567c75e12dee30215a5fc6b121dbd33601/tests/cases/__snapshots__/high-pass-rc-filter-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The comparison includes all 11 components at equal scale, with a divider and red numbered findings. The [original full repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8919d4567c75e12dee30215a5fc6b121dbd33601/tests/cases/__snapshots__/mini-mp3-high-pass-rc-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) remains and now highlights both new findings alongside the existing C44 flip finding. The [complete corrected snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8919d4567c75e12dee30215a5fc6b121dbd33601/tests/cases/__snapshots__/high-pass-rc-filter-correction-full-sheet.snap.svg) has **zero findings from full placement analysis**.

The correction is a hand-arranged TSX example, not an automatic move produced by this analyzer. It groups both pairs, rotates C44 to address the pre-existing flip finding, and aligns the three other output RC branches below. Explicit ground labels keep return wires clear of the signal paths. All components, values, symbol families, and pin connections are preserved; the added ground labels duplicate existing source-trace connections without changing connectivity.

## Detection

- Uses typed capacitors/resistors, connectivity, and explicit ground/power flags. No semantic checks of component names, pin names, hints, or net labels.
- Requires exactly one unambiguous capacitor/resistor/load junction: one capacitor terminal, one resistor terminal, and one local chip or connector terminal represented by a typed `simple_chip`/`simple_op_amp`. The resistor's other terminal must be explicitly grounded, and neither capacitor net may be a known rail.
- Reports excessive shared-pin separation, allowing a gap of at least 4 schematic units or three component dimensions. This is a readability heuristic, not an electrical distance requirement or an exact alignment rule.
- Skips ambiguous branches, feedback to the same host, missing ground metadata, contradictory rails, different sheets/groups, duplicate or missing placements/ports, overlaps, invalid values/geometry, unpopulated parts, and unconnected pins.

## Real source and reference

[mohan-bee/mini-mp3-player v1.2.0](https://tscircuit.com/mohan-bee/mini-mp3-player?version=1.2.0#schematic), release `69ee72ea-36c9-4629-a498-d83692d97817`. The TSX repro preserves the complete 11-component Audio/headphone section. The decoder section and other sheets are outside its scope; the zero-findings result applies to this complete extracted block.

[VLSI Connecting Analog Outputs, Figure 8, page 8](https://www.vlsi.fi/fileadmin/app_notes/vs10XXan_output.pdf#page=8) shows C1 grouped with grounded R4 and C2 with grounded R3. This supports the presentation of the topology; the reference's values are not substituted into the repro.

## Validation

- `bun test`: **231 passing**; `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run build` pass.
- Checks all 24 source ports and 576 pairwise connectivity relationships, unchanged electrical records, normalized source-trace connections, preserved symbols/pin geometry apart from the stated rotations, and continuous drawn wires for both capacitor/resistor joins.
- Guard coverage includes renaming every semantic label, explicit port-ground metadata, missing/contradictory metadata, ambiguous topology, scope, invalid/duplicate geometry, unpopulated parts, overlap, rotation, and the existing low-pass fixture.
- Original full repro and both correction snapshots visually inspected. No unrelated snapshots or dependencies change.
