title: feat: detect misaligned parallel diode capacitor pairs
description: Adds functionality to detect misaligned parallel diode-capacitor pairs in schematic designs, ensuring correct alignment for improved circuit performance.
body:
Adds `ParallelDiodeCapacitorAlignmentSolver` → `ParallelDiodeCapacitorNotAligned`. In [mohan-bee/pcb v1.0.0](https://tscircuit.com/mohan-bee/pcb?version=1.0.0#schematic), D1/CM1 through D4/CM4 each share both nets, but are staggered with corresponding connections at opposite ends. The correction draws each pair as adjacent parallel branches with continuous shared wires.

**Stacked on #290**, which contains only the published TSX repro and its original full-sheet snapshot.

### One motor block

![One complete motor block, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/10f7bad5350c04a9c69c4c1172b5b3e0392f107c/tests/cases/__snapshots__/drone-parallel-diode-capacitor-correction-detail.snap.svg)

### All four motor blocks

![All four complete motor blocks, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/10f7bad5350c04a9c69c4c1172b5b3e0392f107c/tests/cases/__snapshots__/drone-parallel-diode-capacitor-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The comparison uses equal-scale sectional views, a central divider, red numbered markers, and diagnostics underneath. The original placements remain unchanged in the repro.

### Published reference and original schematic

| Published parallel-branch convention | Original complete schematic rendered from TSX |
| --- | --- |
| ![TI parallel diode/capacitor branches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/0cd079b36b45e10a88faf3e89c64b5a4bb84695f/ti-parallel-diode-capacitor-reference.png) | ![Original full-sheet repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/10f7bad5350c04a9c69c4c1172b5b3e0392f107c/tests/cases/__snapshots__/drone-parallel-diode-capacitor-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) |

[TI TIDA-050030, Figure 8, page 12](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/tidueu1a/tidueu1a.pdf#page=12) draws D1 beside C4/C5/C12 with shared top and bottom connections. Its TVS/input-protection application differs from this motor circuit; the reference illustrates the drawing convention, not the diode's electrical function.

### Detection and limits

Uses typed diode/capacitor components, electrical connectivity, and schematic port geometry. An unambiguous local pair sharing two distinct nets is reported for different axes, opposite matching-net directions, or disjoint terminal spans. Horizontal and vertical layouts, unequal symbols, and small offsets are accepted. Names, labels, and `port_hints` do not establish roles.

Skips pairs whose two nets are explicitly supply/ground rails, since those rails can join unrelated functional blocks. Also skips distant parts, different scopes/sheets, ambiguous banks, overlapping bodies, unplaced/disconnected parts, and missing or invalid geometry. Locality is a symbol-size tolerance, not a physical design rule. This analyzer reports advice; the corrected TSX demonstrates the proposed placement.

| Layout | Existing findings | New pair findings |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original full sheet | 4 | 4 |
| Existing findings corrected, motor pairs unchanged | 0 | 4 |
| Complete corrected sheet | 0 | 0 |

### Complete correction

All **58 components** remain. The four motor blocks form a compact 2×2 arrangement; diode rotation keeps every pin connection and polarity intact. The full-sheet fixture also groups the supply capacitors, shortens the flagged rail paths, and repositions programming points. These moves resolve the four existing findings. Symbols and chip pin layouts are preserved.

<details>
<summary>Complete corrected sheet — four broad sections, zero full-analysis findings</summary>

![Complete corrected schematic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/10f7bad5350c04a9c69c4c1172b5b3e0392f107c/tests/cases/__snapshots__/drone-parallel-diode-capacitor-correction-full-sheet.snap.svg)

</details>

### Validation

- **232 tests pass**; typecheck, formatting, and browser build pass.
- Tests assert unchanged source electrical records, all components and pin geometry, and continuous drawn wires between both terminals of every pair.
- Coverage includes rotation/translation, anonymous labels, valid layouts, shared supply rails, ambiguous banks, and incomplete metadata.
- Visually inspected the original, both comparisons, and the complete corrected snapshot. Only this repro's original snapshot gains findings; no unrelated snapshots, dependencies, or timeouts change.

description: Adds ParallelLedBranchPlacementSolver for complete parallel resistorLED branches drawn end-to-end in the same row or column, reporting grouped findings for such configurations.
body:
Adds `ParallelLedBranchPlacementSolver` → `ParallelLedBranchesDrawnInline` for complete parallel resistor/LED branches drawn end-to-end in the same row or column. On [Devesh36/bicycle-brake-light v0.1.3](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/bicycle-brake-light?version=0.1.3#schematic), it reports one grouped finding covering all six branches.

Stacked on repro **#287**.

![Complete Lights sheet before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/c6daf0b45e293496a7cc0c604ebc1d6c00c51924/tests/cases/__snapshots__/parallel-led-branch-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The manual TSX correction draws the six branches beside each other with continuous shared rails, and fixes the seven existing rail-orientation findings and the gate-network finding. **Full analysis of the complete corrected Lights sheet reports 0 findings.** The analyzer reports advice; it does not move components automatically.

All 15 components remain. Tests verify identical source components, ports, nets, traces, groups and internal connections; the original symbols and pin geometry are preserved, allowing placement rotations. They also verify continuous rendered wires through each resistor/LED pair, both shared buses, and the gate network. `schMaxTraceDistance={30}` allows the renderer to draw the complete buses; no source traces are added. Q1's original symbol and pin arrangement remain unchanged.

[Original complete sheet with the new finding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/c6daf0b45e293496a7cc0c604ebc1d6c00c51924/tests/cases/__snapshots__/bicycle-brake-light-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) · [Complete corrected sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/c6daf0b45e293496a7cc0c604ebc1d6c00c51924/tests/cases/__snapshots__/parallel-led-branch-correction-full-sheet.snap.svg)

| Lights-sheet state | Existing findings | New bank finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original placements | 8 | 1 |
| Existing findings fixed; branches remain end-to-end | 0 | 1 |
| Branches also arranged in parallel | 0 | 0 |

![Existing findings fixed, with the new branch arrangement finding still present](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/c6daf0b45e293496a7cc0c604ebc1d6c00c51924/tests/cases/__snapshots__/parallel-led-branch-correction-existing-findings-fixed-comparison.snap.svg)

The control demonstrates an independent coverage gap. Existing diode/resistor alignment checks one pair, series-LED analysis checks a series chain, and parallel-resistor analysis checks individual resistors sharing both nets. Here each resistor has a private junction with its own LED, while the **complete branches** share the two end nets.

Detection requires at least three typed resistor/LED branches, private intermediate junctions, two shared outer nets, and a common local scope. One outer net must be a local node not explicitly marked as a supply/ground, with at most one additional local terminal. Shared supply rails alone do not group unrelated indicators. Names, labels, hints and part numbers are not used to infer roles. Ambiguous geometry, tapped junctions, separate returns, DNP/disconnected parts, zero-ohm resistors, and mixed sheets/groups are skipped. Side-by-side placements and modest offsets are accepted; exact alignment is unnecessary.

| Published Kingbright reference | Original Lights sheet from TSX |
| --- | --- |
| ![Kingbright parallel LED branches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/1aa3d53d880f623765ad94d8b4b43fd72b48f741/kingbright-parallel-led-branches.png) | ![Original complete Lights sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/c6daf0b45e293496a7cc0c604ebc1d6c00c51924/tests/cases/__snapshots__/bicycle-brake-light-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) |

[Kingbright, Application Notes for SMD LEDs, page 6](https://www.kingbrightusa.com/applicationnotes/ApplicationNotesFor_SMD_LEDs.pdf#page=6), shows the parallel-branch convention. The original circuit already satisfies its electrical advice to give each LED a resistor. This analyzer concerns readability, not electrical correctness or a manufacturer spacing limit.

Validation: **232 tests pass**, typecheck and formatting pass. The first full run hit two existing Stride-test timeouts; an unchanged standalone rerun passed all tests. Coverage includes all cardinal rotations, translation, accepted offsets, anonymous metadata, topology/geometry guards, unchanged source records, and wire continuity. title: feat: detect resistors separated from crystals
description: Adds CrystalResistorPlacementSolver to detect when a crystals series resistor is placed far from its shared crystal branch, improving schematic placement analysis.
body:
Adds `CrystalResistorPlacementSolver` → `ResistorSeparatedFromCrystal` for a crystal's series resistor placed far from its shared crystal branch. On [Devesh36/pocket-audio-player v1.0.12](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/pocket-audio-player?version=1.0.12#schematic), the complete Clock sheet now reports the separated `R_XOUT` resistor as well as its pre-existing ground-route finding.

Stacked on repro **#283**.

![Complete Clock sheet before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8b35585719247131610d5c9e3a73f51438db9011/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pocket-audio-crystal-resistor-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The manual TSX correction moves and rotates `R_XOUT` beside `Y1`, then moves the two load capacitors nearby to clear the pre-existing ground-route issue. **Full placement analysis of the complete corrected Clock sheet reports 0 findings.** The analyzer reports advice; it does not move components automatically.

All five components remain. Tests verify unchanged electrical source records, values, native symbols and pin geometry (allowing the resistor's 180° rotation), and a continuous rendered wire between the resistor and crystal. No chip pin layout changes are made. The comparison uses equal scale, a vertical divider, red numbered markers and diagnostics below; the original full sheet is retained and gains the new finding.

[Original full sheet with both findings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8b35585719247131610d5c9e3a73f51438db9011/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pocket-audio-crystal-resistor-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) · [Complete corrected full sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8b35585719247131610d5c9e3a73f51438db9011/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pocket-audio-crystal-resistor-correction-full-sheet.snap.svg)

| Clock-sheet layout | Existing findings | New resistor finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original placements | 1 ground-route finding | 1 |
| Only the capacitors moved; resistor unchanged | 0 | 1 |
| Resistor and capacitors grouped | 0 | 0 |

The capacitor-only test demonstrates the coverage gap independently of the existing finding. `ChipPinResistorPlacementSolver` handles a private chip-to-ground resistor, while this resistor lies in a crystal signal branch. Existing crystal rules do not check its separation.

Detection uses typed crystal/resistor/capacitor components, connectivity, explicit ground/power metadata and local geometry. One crystal signal terminal connects through the resistor to a chip; the other connects directly to that same chip. Grounded load capacitors are allowed. Unknown four-pin terminal roles, extra signal branches, parallel/shorted resistor paths, rail connections, DNP/disconnected parts, different local scopes and missing or ambiguous geometry are skipped. Names and hints are used only in displayed diagnostics. The distance tolerance allows label space; it is a schematic readability heuristic, not an electrical design limit.

[Raspberry Pi's Hardware design with RP2040, Figure 8 (printed page 9 / PDF page 10)](https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2040/hardware-design-with-rp2040.pdf#page=10) supplies the reference: R5 (1 kΩ) is drawn beside the crystal's branch. Its orientation is not mandatory.

| Published Raspberry Pi reference | Original complete Clock sheet from TSX |
| --- | --- |
| ![Figure 8: RP2040 crystal circuit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/0918551416e4996a553a6e2d232af55dc56f127e/rp2040-figure8.png) | ![Original complete Clock sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8b35585719247131610d5c9e3a73f51438db9011/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pocket-audio-crystal-resistor-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) |

Validation: **231 tests pass**, typecheck and formatting pass. Coverage includes two-/four-pin crystals, rotation, either signal arm, accepted nearby/offset placements, anonymous names, topology and metadata guards, unchanged connectivity and wire continuity. All three SVGs were rendered and inspected. No unrelated snapshots or dependencies changed.

body:
**Motivation:** Refresh all six TI Altium samples (`sample021`–`sample026`) from their SHA-256-pinned sources using released converter updates, so the saved routing inputs reflect the boards' declared routing constraints.

**Actual:** The stored samples use `altium-to-circuit-json` 0.0.75. Their SRJs default to a 0.1 mm minimum trace width, omit source via pad/hole diameter limits, and disable blind/buried vias for every board. The saved Circuit JSON also lacks the CAD bodies preserved by the newer importer.

**Expected / fix:** Pin `altium-to-circuit-json` 0.0.106, `altiumts` 0.0.94, core 0.0.2165, Circuit JSON 0.0.528, and `circuit-to-svg` 0.0.450, then regenerate all six Circuit JSON files, SRJs, and comparison SVGs. The generator uses the public byte-input conversion API so parser objects do not cross different installed `altiumts` instances. Update the six README connection counts.

The regenerated SRJs retain the source's 0.1524 mm minimum trace width and board-specific via dimensions; `sample023` and `sample024` now allow blind/buried vias. Source hashes, obstacle geometry, connection counts, and endpoint definitions are unchanged across all six boards. The refreshed Circuit JSON adds 1,899 CAD component records and nine fabrication-note paths.

**Validation:**

- Generate all six boards with `bun run generate:ti --source-root <verified-source-root>`; every source hash and generated Circuit JSON element passes validation.
- `bun run test`: 26 samples and 858 through-hole obstacles validated.
- `bun run build`: passes.
- All six regenerated samples have finite, noncollapsed rectangular obstacle bounds with dimensions above `1e-9` mm.
- Pipeline 9 with autorouter 0.0.985 and `effort: 0.1` completes all 16 point-pair routes for regenerated `sample023` without an error. This is a focused smoke test, not a full routing benchmark of all six boards.
- Rendered and visually inspected all six comparison SVGs; `git diff --check` passes.

**Related:** Consumes released [Altium routing-constraint support](https://github.com/tscircuit/altium-to-circuit-json/pull/186) and [primitive 3D body support](https://github.com/tscircuit/altium-to-circuit-json/pull/208). Overlaps the routing-metadata regeneration in [dataset-srj24 #8](https://github.com/tscircuit/dataset-srj24/pull/8), and builds on main after the merged [sample024 keepout regeneration #14](https://github.com/tscircuit/dataset-srj24/pull/14). Samples 001–020 are unchanged.

body:
Sample024’s five open keepout arcs expand into 1,430 SRJ obstacles; this PR regenerates them as 475 native rotated rectangles and square joins/caps and updates the SRJ comparison panel.
It pins the official releases `@tscircuit/core@0.0.2163` from merged [core #4669](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4669) and `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter@0.0.985` containing merged [autorouter #3098](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3098), with integrity recorded in `bun.lock`.

title: fix: preserve valid offset rails during pair shortening
description: Stacked on 58, targeting its repro branch. A routable near-horizontal pair can return null when centerline shortening reverses one offset rail and creates a 135 corner. Add an optional validity predicate to the ordinary reducer and check conventional turns and self-clearance on both paired rails. Shortcuts preserve already-valid rails while allowing progressive repair of initially invalid paths. Ordinary callers retain their behavior and final routing validation remains in place. Add the exact repro as coupled-offset-shortening, the twelfth case in both the default CLI benchmark and the shared main-versus-PR manifest. It routes through each selected revisions public pipeline, with independent requirements for 2 signals, no fixed copper or buses, and one matched pair. The eleven AM3352 cases retain their original 47-signal161-fixed-fanout checks. Tests cover revision selection, failedcontradictory solver states, missing cases, strict reports and completion statistics. Validation: Original repro unchanged: 3 tests  86 assertions pass. Current benchmarkregression suite: 35 tests  987 assertions across 7 files pass; type checking and the full 338-file format check pass. The actual new benchmark worker fails on pre-fix revision 7726294 with coupled_routing_failed (02 signals), and passes on the fix (22, full DRCconnectivitycouplingmatching, 0 mm pair skew, 68.263 ms solve). A fresh AM3352 control run passes 4747 signals with full DRCmatching and all 161 fixed fanouts preserved: 42.978 s solve. Total-copper byte-bus skews are approximately 0.635 mm; pair skews are 0.077868, 0.126884 and 0.072830 mm. The prior completed eleven-case AM3352 run and all eleven inspected PNGs remain unchanged. A separate fully validated reduced-case PNGSVG and native worker report are added; its PNG was opened and inspected. See measurements, native reports and completed snapshots(https:github.comtscircuitbus-lanes-solverblobd61928ea9b2ab6640b06932d10fdcf25b3dbcdc0docscoupled-offset-shortening-fixREADME.md). The historical eleven-case run is not presented as a newly rerun twelve-case aggregate. Its mixed GC settings remain documented, and its original JSON capture stays byte-for-byte intact. GitHub benchmark uses the trusted default-branch harness: it will include the new case after this harnessmanifest change reaches main.
body:
Stacked on #58, targeting its repro branch.

A routable near-horizontal pair can return `null` when centerline shortening reverses one offset rail and creates a 135° corner. Add an optional validity predicate to the ordinary reducer and check conventional turns and self-clearance on both paired rails. Shortcuts preserve already-valid rails while allowing progressive repair of initially invalid paths. Ordinary callers retain their behavior and final routing validation remains in place.

Add the exact repro as `coupled-offset-shortening`, the twelfth case in both the default CLI benchmark and the shared main-versus-PR manifest. It routes through each selected revision's public pipeline, with independent requirements for 2 signals, no fixed copper or buses, and one matched pair. The eleven AM3352 cases retain their original 47-signal/161-fixed-fanout checks. Tests cover revision selection, failed/contradictory solver states, missing cases, strict reports and completion statistics.

Validation:

- Original repro unchanged: 3 tests / 86 assertions pass.
- Current benchmark/regression suite: 35 tests / 987 assertions across 7 files pass; type checking and the full 338-file format check pass.
- The actual new benchmark worker fails on pre-fix revision `7726294` with `coupled_routing_failed` (0/2 signals), and passes on the fix (2/2, full DRC/connectivity/coupling/matching, 0 mm pair skew, 68.263 ms solve).
- A fresh AM3352 control run passes 47/47 signals with full DRC/matching and all 161 fixed fanouts preserved: 42.978 s solve. Total-copper byte-bus skews are approximately 0.635 mm; pair skews are 0.077868, 0.126884 and 0.072830 mm.
- The prior completed eleven-case AM3352 run and all eleven inspected PNGs remain unchanged. A separate fully validated reduced-case PNG/SVG and native worker report are added; its PNG was opened and inspected.

See [measurements, native reports and completed snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/d61928ea9b2ab6640b06932d10fdcf25b3dbcdc0/docs/coupled-offset-shortening-fix/README.md). The historical eleven-case run is not presented as a newly rerun twelve-case aggregate. Its mixed GC settings remain documented, and its original JSON capture stays byte-for-byte intact.

GitHub `/benchmark` uses the trusted default-branch harness: it will include the new case after this harness/manifest change reaches `main`.

title: Add NEMA23 DRV8452 C firmware and power controls
description: The published NEMA23 1.3.2 board has a different driver, GPIO map, current scale and power interlocks from the DRV8825 controller. Add a separate MOTOR_BOARDnema23_drv8452 native C target and matching controls on the bench, single-motor and gantry pages. This PR is based on 16s current-capture work. The profile uses the published STEPDIRSPIRGBbuzzer wiring, nominal 0.2 VA current sensing, a conservative 1 A peak current default and a verified fixed 116 driver configuration. Both regular telemetry and high-rate graph frames use the boards current scale. Driver SPI is checked with ARM low before motion; fault clearing is limited to explicit power arming. Sensorless stall detection and the DNP encoder are not enabled. POWER_ARMARMWAKEbuffer enable boot low. Voltage changes isolate and discharge the rail for 12 seconds, then require fresh PD communicationprotocolcurrent checks. PG is ignored by default so a deasserted signal cannot prevent the first software voltage request. The UI exposes optional strict PG gating, and changing it disarms the rail. Raw PG telemetry remains separate from the override and measured voltage remains unavailable. Power needs explicit arming below 55C; 60C folds current back and 70C or sensoreFusedriverSPI failure latches off the rail. HeartbeatUSB loss disarms. The buffer is disabled after disarm, communication failure or any latched fault. Validation: Both ARM targets built; UBSan motionprotocolsettingscurrent and new production NEMA23 parserpowerSPI tests passed. All 45 Python regressions and dashboardjogpositionssongcurrent-graphcontrol tests passed. CI builds both board profiles and runs ASanUBSan. Flashed two physical NEMA23 controllers. The second (e6658c344b0a562a) is connected to a motor and reported healthy temperaturecurrent sensing, approximately 100k ADC samplessec per winding, a 1 A peak default, and disabled motorpower rail. Driver-disabled PIO tests emitted exact counts at 1k64k200k settings with zero queue underruns while current data streamed. With PG ignored, the second board completed a 15 V request and reported a 3 A PD contract. Protected-rail and SPI readback checks passed. At a 1 A peak limit it completed ten full steps forward and ten back (18 commanded each way) at 20 full stepssec, with 160 counted pulses each direction and about 0.7 A measured in an energized winding. The user confirmed seeing forwardreverse motion. Test ended stopped and disarmed. Actual rail voltage, calibrated current and loaded positional accuracy remain unmeasured. Matching UI deployed to https:motorcontrol.tscircuit.com; explicit armcurrent controls preserve legacy board behavior.
body:
The published NEMA23 1.3.2 board has a different driver, GPIO map, current scale and power interlocks from the DRV8825 controller. Add a separate `MOTOR_BOARD=nema23_drv8452` native C target and matching controls on the bench, single-motor and gantry pages. This PR is based on #16's current-capture work.

The profile uses the published STEP/DIR/SPI/RGB/buzzer wiring, nominal 0.2 V/A current sensing, a conservative 1 A peak current default and a verified fixed 1/16 driver configuration. Both regular telemetry and high-rate graph frames use the board's current scale. Driver SPI is checked with ARM low before motion; fault clearing is limited to explicit power arming. Sensorless stall detection and the DNP encoder are not enabled.

POWER_ARM/ARM/WAKE/buffer enable boot low. Voltage changes isolate and discharge the rail for 12 seconds, then require fresh PD communication/protocol/current checks. PG is ignored by default so a deasserted signal cannot prevent the first software voltage request. The UI exposes optional strict PG gating, and changing it disarms the rail. Raw PG telemetry remains separate from the override and measured voltage remains unavailable. Power needs explicit arming below 55°C; 60°C folds current back and 70°C or sensor/eFuse/driver/SPI failure latches off the rail. Heartbeat/USB loss disarms. The buffer is disabled after disarm, communication failure or any latched fault.

Validation:
- Both ARM targets built; UBSan motion/protocol/settings/current and new production NEMA23 parser/power/SPI tests passed. All 45 Python regressions and dashboard/jog/positions/song/current-graph/control tests passed. CI builds both board profiles and runs ASan/UBSan.
- Flashed two physical NEMA23 controllers. The second (`e6658c344b0a562a`) is connected to a motor and reported healthy temperature/current sensing, approximately 100k ADC samples/sec per winding, a 1 A peak default, and disabled motor/power rail. Driver-disabled PIO tests emitted exact counts at 1k/64k/200k settings with zero queue underruns while current data streamed.
- With PG ignored, the second board completed a 15 V request and reported a 3 A PD contract. Protected-rail and SPI readback checks passed. At a 1 A peak limit it completed ten full steps forward and ten back (18° commanded each way) at 20 full steps/sec, with 160 counted pulses each direction and about 0.7 A measured in an energized winding. The user confirmed seeing forward/reverse motion. Test ended stopped and disarmed. Actual rail voltage, calibrated current and loaded positional accuracy remain unmeasured.
- Matching UI deployed to https://motorcontrol.tscircuit.com; explicit arm/current controls preserve legacy board behavior.

title: Show high-rate winding current graphs on all motor pages
description: Add winding-current graphs to the bench, single-motor and gantry pages, backed by native ADCDMA capture at 100,000 samplessec per winding. The browser shows ten seconds of signed current, preserving peak ranges and weighted averages without streaming every raw reading. Legacy firmware falls back to regular telemetry.
body:
Add winding-current graphs to the bench, single-motor and gantry pages, backed by native ADC/DMA capture at 100,000 samples/sec per winding. The browser shows ten seconds of signed current, preserving peak ranges and weighted averages without streaming every raw reading. Legacy firmware falls back to regular telemetry.

Capture runs independently of PIO pulse generation. USB frames carry 1 ms min/max/sum/count bins, hardware timestamps and skipped-sample counts; bounded output reserves space for commands and protection telemetry. Graph history is bounded, ADC errors/clipping remain gaps, and queued frames after reconnect cannot push the timeline into the future. Readings are uncalibrated winding currents, not supply current.

Validation: ARM UF2 build and native UBSan checks passed; all 45 Python tests and dashboard, gantry, single-motor, positions, song and new graph checks passed. Both physical controllers were flashed and measured approximately 100k samples/sec per winding. Driver-disabled tests at 1k/64k/128k/200k pulse settings emitted exact counts with zero PIO queue underruns (about 199.7k pulses/sec at the maximum setting). Live readings were verified on all three production pages. No loaded motor movement or calibrated current measurement was tested.

Deployed to https://motorcontrol.tscircuit.com.

title: Add native C firmware with PIO step generation
description: DRV8825 controllers currently generate STEP edges in MicroPython, so higher requested speeds can exceed the interpreters pulse throughput. Add a native Pico SDK C application that generates pulses in PIO and counts emitted edges with a separate PIO state machine and DMA. The application retains protocol 3, the existing dashboardgantry commands, 400 ms ramps, deferred GOTO starts, RGBUSB-PD controls, alarms, songs, and temperaturedriverheartbeatwatchdog protections. Native settings use two reserved flash sectors with checksum and partial-write recovery. A build fingerprint identifies the image on live boards. The legacy DRV8847 MicroPython implementation remains available; this native image targets the DRV8825RGB PCB. Validation: Cross-built the UF2 with Pico SDK 2.3.1; native motion, protocolprotection, and settings tests passed with UBSan. Existing 45 Python tests and dashboard, song, single-motor, gantry, and saved-position checks passed. Flashed both physical controllers and checked their build fingerprints. Driver-disabled electrical tests emitted exact requested counts at 1k, 64k, 128k, and 200k physical pulsessec with zero PIO queue underruns. At the 200k setting, observed throughput was approximately 199.7k pulsessec on both boards. Verified heartbeat expiry and USB disconnect stop pulse generation, heartbeats do not resume it, settings survive restart, and restarts return to disabled 5 V with fresh position sessions. No shaft movement or loaded mechanical performance was tested. Independent pulse-widthjitter measurement, loaded torque, and physical positional accuracy remain unverified. CI adds host native tests and an ARM UF2 build.

title: Support the RP2040 DRV8825 and RGB controller board
description: The latest RP2040 motor controller uses DRV8825 STEPDIR, transistor-driven RGB outputs, winding-current ADC inputs and GPIO-controlled CH224K voltage selection. Voltage changes disable the driver and enforce a settling interval; temperature, heartbeat, watchdog and driver-fault protection remain active. Automatic RGB status and manual colors are available, with alarms taking priority. The hardware fixes 116 microsteps; larger selected increments group pulses and saved-position GOTO uses the finest supported increment. Validation: 45 Python tests and all dashboardjogGOTOsong checks pass; CI stages both board profiles. On board e66568714f117e21, all 21 uploaded files matched SHA-256. Live Web Serial controls applied RGB settings and the user confirmed LED operation. With the replacement charger and an explicit 9 V request, two 800-microstep forwardreverse moves completed with exact commanded counts, about 0.87 A peak absolute winding samples and no reported faults; the user confirmed the motor spun. Temperature stayed around 28 C and the motor was stopped afterward. Use 9 V with the tested charger. A 15 V request yielded a measured 9 V input and no movement; the actual PG behavior was not measured. Voltage telemetry represents the request and settling timer, not measured rail voltage. Current samples are uncalibrated, and high-speedloadphysical return accuracy remain unverified.

Startup keeps the motor disabled at 5 V. Voltage changes disable the driver and enforce a settling interval; temperature, heartbeat, watchdog and driver-fault protection remain active. Automatic RGB status and manual colors are available, with alarms taking priority. The hardware fixes 1/16 microsteps; larger selected increments group pulses and saved-position GOTO uses the finest supported increment.

Validation: 45 Python tests and all dashboard/jog/GOTO/song checks pass; CI stages both board profiles. On board e66568714f117e21, all 21 uploaded files matched SHA-256. title: Expose quarter and microstep controls on single-motor jogging
description: The single-motor jogging page now exposes supported quarter, 18 and 116 step sizes with angular increments and RPM estimates. Speed labels follow the selected increment, and saved-position GOTO converts that speed to its finest supported increment so changing step size does not silently change return speed.
body:
The single-motor jogging page now exposes supported quarter, 1/8 and 1/16 step sizes with angular increments and RPM estimates. Speed labels follow the selected increment, and saved-position GOTO converts that speed to its finest supported increment so changing step size does not silently change return speed.

The page also displays winding-current samples alongside USB-PD and RGB controls. Requested and measured PD voltage are separated. Measured voltage remains unavailable on the existing v1.0.42 board: R_PD_VBUS feeds CH224K VBUS, while the RP2040's ADC-capable pins serve temperature I2C and winding current. Actual voltage telemetry from future hardware is displayed when provided.

Validation: all existing Python and dashboard/jog/GOTO/song checks pass. Single-page regressions cover quarter/microstep commands, angular/RPM labels, RGB/voltage commands, stale/motion gating, legacy boards, exact microstep GOTO coordinates and speed conversion, and requested-versus-measured voltage handling.

title: Add symbol contain fitting and local viewbox bounds (#4698)
description: Adds optional fit modes and viewbox bounds to symbol properties, allowing for better control over symbol sizing and proportions.
body:
Custom symbols need a way to preserve their proportions during sizing and define their own source bounds. Adds optional `fit="fill" | "contain" | "stretch"` and `viewbox={{ minX, maxX, minY, maxY }}` to the public symbol props and runtime validation, enabling tscircuit/core#4706.

`contain` requests uniform scaling; CSS-style `fill` and explicit `stretch` retain independent scaling. Viewbox bounds use the local symbol coordinate space (mm, +X right, +Y up), accept numbers or distance strings, and require `maxX > minX` and `maxY > minY`. Existing defaults are preserved. Generated API documentation is included.

Follows Seve’s [fit-mode review](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/943#discussion_r4300043097) and [min/max bounds review](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/943#discussion_r4300047578).

Validation: all 683 tests, full TypeScript checking, package/declaration build, and all four documentation generators pass. The current PR head has the same Git tree as the validated fix. Hosted test, typecheck, formatting, and package-preview checks are green.

Includes the fix already merged in #943. This PR targets `main` and now contains both the repro tests and their implementation, with ordinary passing assertions. After it lands and a props release is published, core#4706 can replace its preview dependency with that published version.

title: Add symbol contain fitting and an explicit local viewbox (#4698)
description: Adds optional custom-symbol fit modes and viewbox properties for improved symbol rendering in local coordinate space.
body:
Adds optional custom-symbol `fit="fill" | "contain" | "stretch"` and `viewbox={{ minX, maxX, minY, maxY }}` props for core#4698. This PR defines the TypeScript and validation boundary with generated documentation; core#4706 implements the geometry.

Follows Seve’s [fit-mode review](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/943#discussion_r4300043097), [min/max viewbox review](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/943#discussion_r4300047578), and [local-symbol-coordinate wording](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4706#discussion_r4300040219).

`contain` scales uniformly to preserve proportions. CSS-style `fill` and explicit `stretch` scale axes independently, preserving the existing default. The viewbox defines source bounds in the local symbol coordinate space (mm, +X right, +Y up). During width/height sizing its center maps to the symbol position, with artwork and ports receiving the same transform. All four bounds are required; numbers and unit-aware distance strings are accepted and parsed to mm. `maxX` must exceed `minX`, and `maxY` must exceed `minY`.

For a round contact with a 1 mm body centered at the local origin:
```tsx
<symbol
  width={2}
  fit="contain"
  viewbox={{ minX: -0.5, maxX: 0.5, minY: -0.5, maxY: 0.5 }}
>
  {/* round contact drawing and connection port */}
</symbol>
```
The body scales to a 2 mm circle even when a port stem extends outside those source bounds. Omitted viewbox retains automatic artwork-plus-port bounds. With no requested width/height, rendering stays unchanged. There are no alternate prop spellings or alternate viewbox object shapes.

Validation: all three repro assertions fail on unchanged props and pass with the fix. All 683 tests, TypeScript checking, and the package/declaration build pass. All four required generation scripts ran; generated changes are included. Hosted props CI passes. Seve’s props#810 concrete-use-case request and core#2607/#3208 source-geometry/defined-port guidance remain respected.

Stack: [repro #942](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/942) → [fix #943](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/943). Merge the repro first, then retarget the fix to `main`.

title: repro: printedpart color is ignored by JSCAD renderer
description: Fixes the issue where the printedpart color prop is ignored in the JSCAD renderer, causing discrepancies in color rendering for CAD components.
body:
While building [Done Dot](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/done-dot#3d), its red status lens appeared gray in the JSCAD renderer.

This story creates two identical cylinders using `<assembly.printedpart color="#d73e39">`. Both should be red. The left cylinder renders gray; the right renders red because its geometry also uses `<jscad.colorize>`. The circuit JSON comes directly from `circuit.getCircuitJson()` without modification.

**[Open the Storybook repro](https://3d-viewer-git-fork-devesh36-repro-assembly-jsc-883497-tscircuit.vercel.app/?path=/story/bugs-printedpartcolorignored--same-red-color)** — the story opens the JSCAD renderer directly, independent of saved viewer settings.

![The printedpart color prop is ignored on the left; JSCAD colorize works on the right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/3d-viewer/4336560cc4bf5254fc2d4a14a5dd66263ac1f52d/stories/Bugs/__snapshots__/PrintedPartColorIgnored.png)

Color is supported in the Circuit JSON schema as an explicit CAD geometry override. Update the existing development dependencies to core `^0.0.2152` and props `^0.0.701` so the story can use the printedpart color prop directly. The newer core also requires modelprinter `^0.0.18` for its `getJstMotorConnector` export.

Validation: typechecking, the package build, and story formatting pass. Checked that both generated CAD records contain `color: "#d73e39"`, and captured the failure in a fresh browser session. The only browser console error was a missing local Storybook favicon (404).

This PR contains the TSX story, its snapshot, and the development dependency updates needed to run it. It does not change renderer behavior.

title: Preserve custom symbol proportions and local viewbox sizing (#4698)
description: Fixes symbol rendering by preserving custom proportions and local viewbox sizing for schematic symbols, ensuring correct scaling behavior for various fit modes.
body:
Uses published `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.704`, which includes the symbol props from merged props#942/#943. Both the development dependency and override use the published version.

This PR targets `main` and includes the fix already merged through #4706 into this branch.

Fixes #4698 with `fit="fill" | "contain" | "stretch"` and optional `viewbox={{ minX, maxX, minY, maxY }}` source bounds. Contain scales both axes uniformly; CSS-style fill and explicit stretch use independent scale factors. Existing defaults retain independent scaling and automatic port-inclusive bounds.

Follows Seve’s [fit-mode review](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/943#discussion_r4300043097), [min/max viewbox review](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/943#discussion_r4300047578), and [local-symbol-coordinate naming](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4706#discussion_r4300040219).

The cached bounds property is named `schematicSymbolBoundsInSymbolLocalCoordinateSpace` in both `Symbol.ts` and `ISymbol.ts`, following Seve’s naming review.

The viewbox establishes the local symbol coordinate space (mm, +X right, +Y up). Core translates those min/max bounds into the pre-resize schematic world frame used by child geometry. During width/height sizing the source bounds center maps to the symbol position. Artwork and ports share that transform, including ports outside the source bounds. With no requested width/height, rendering stays unchanged. The sizing transform composes before the rotation in existing PR #4704.

Validation: all five ordinary regressions fail on unchanged core and pass with this fix. The existing all-primitives resize control passes too (6 focused tests total). Full TypeScript checking and the repository dependency guard pass against the installed published props release. Fixtures use round contacts with a cross; the new fit-mode snapshot was rendered and visually inspected. Hosted CI is green, including all ten test shards, typechecking, formatting, and the distribution smoke test.

Seve’s #2607/#3208 source-geometry and defined-port guidance is followed. Existing merged #4130/#4580 body and routing bounds behavior is preserved. No CI coverage changes.

The fix PR #4706 has already been merged into this branch. This PR now contains the passing regression tests and implementation together. Merging this PR to `main` is the remaining step before publishing core with the fix for eval.

![Fill, stretch, and contain on a round contact](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/fix/symbol-contain/tests/components/primitive-components/__snapshots__/custom-symbol-contain-fit-modes-schematic.snap.svg)

The viewbox establishes the local symbol coordinate space (mm, +X right, +Y up). Core translates those min/max bounds into the pre-resize schematic world frame used by child geometry. During width/height sizing the source bounds center maps to the symbol position. Artwork and ports share that transform, including ports outside the source bounds. With no requested width/height, rendering stays unchanged. The sizing transform composes before the rotation in existing PR #4704.

Validation: all five ordinary regressions fail on unchanged core and pass with this fix. The existing all-primitives resize control passes too (6 focused tests total). Full TypeScript checking and the repository dependency guard pass against the installed published props release. Fixtures use round contacts with a cross; the new fit-mode snapshot was rendered and visually inspected. Hosted CI is rerunning for the published dependency update.

Seve’s #2607/#3208 source-geometry and defined-port guidance is followed. Existing merged #4130/#4580 body and routing bounds behavior is preserved. No CI coverage changes.

This branch includes current upstream main. No dependency changes.

title: fix: include source MPN in BOM Comment
description: Uses the source components manufacturer part number as a fallback for BOM Comment when no resolved MPN is available, ensuring part identity is retained in the assembly BOM.
body:
## Motivation

A source component can specify a manufacturer part number, but BOM generation currently ignores it when no part resolver supplies an MPN. In the published `gokul/mpu6050-mini` board, U1 has `manufacturer_part_number: "MPU-6050"` and JLCPCB part `C24112`; the exported BOM leaves **Comment** blank. This makes the assembly BOM lose the chip's part identity even though it is present in Circuit JSON.

## Change

Use the source component's manufacturer part number as the BOM Comment fallback when the resolved part has no MPN. A resolved MPN still takes priority, and components without either MPN keep their existing value fallback.

Before: `U1` → Comment `""`, Value `C24112`  
After: `U1` → Comment `MPU-6050`, Value `C24112`

Converting its Circuit JSON to a BOM without a part resolver preserves the supplier number but leaves U1's **Comment** blank. The exported BOM loses a part identity already present in the design.

title: fix: preserve QFP thermal-pad copper connectivity
description: Fixes copper connectivity issues for QFP thermal pads, ensuring proper routing and obstacle handling in autorouting.
body:
QFP thermal-pad topology drops the pad's `connectedTo` aliases. When topology merging splits an exposed pad around an embedded trace target, the surrounding copper has no net owner and TinyHypergraph removes it as a full obstacle. This isolates U5 EP in bugreport109 (#3088) and fails static reachability for `source_net_0_mst26 (pcb_port_417->pcb_port_403)`.

Preserve connectivity on occupied pad layers, matching the existing QFP topology solver. Free layers remain unowned. A small regression exercises topology merging → port graph → TinyHypergraph pathing and verifies each copper pad keeps its own owner.

The full bugreport109 test now requires a successful solve, matches every requested endpoint pair against the emitted traces, and replaces the failure-state snapshot with the final routed board using the repository's computed relaxed-DRC overlay.

![Successfully routed bugreport109 — Relaxed DRC errors: 0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/fix/qfp-thermal-pad-net-connectivity/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport109-book-reading-clip-lamp.snap.svg)

Validation:
- The small regression fails with the original static-reachability error before the fix and passes afterward.
- Existing thermal topology snapshot passes unchanged; build passes.
- Full bugreport109, Pipeline 9, effort 1, cache disabled: 349 output traces covering all endpoint pairs and zero relaxed DRC errors, including trace-continuity checks.
- Regenerated only the bugreport109 snapshot with `BUN_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bun test --timeout 9999999 tests/bugs/bugreport109-book-reading-clip-lamp.test.ts`.

The seven-line production change is entirely in the topology generator.

CI runtime: the full-board test took 542.9 seconds on the Linux runner, exceeding the workflow's five-minute default. It now has an explicit 15-minute timeout. The Linux runner also produces a different valid routing variant; the inspected zero-DRC result from [the CI artifact](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/39044918295/artifacts/12106435436) is recorded as a separate Linux snapshot, following the existing bug-report pattern. Endpoint assertions and snapshot comparison tolerances are unchanged.

title: Add /benchmark --threads for per-sample Pipeline9 workers
description: Adds the ability to specify the number of routing threads per sample for Pipeline9 in the benchmarking process, allowing for improved concurrency and resource management during routing tasks.
body:
Depends on #3125; stacked to keep the benchmark changes separate. Merge that PR first, then retarget this PR to main.

`/benchmark --pipeline 9 --dataset srj18 --threads 4` gives each sample four Bun routing workers. `--threads 1` runs inline. With N > 1, sample concurrency is capped by CPUs / (N + 1), the requested concurrency, and the existing 6 GiB per-sample memory budget (minimum one sample). Omitting the flag preserves existing concurrency overrides. Reports record thread and sample counts.

The shell and workflow inputs forward the flag. The controller builds workers once before samples start; each sample owns/disposes its pool, with startup and disposal included in timing. Unsupported pipelines, networked routing, and threaded profiling reject the combination. Worker failures fail the sample rather than retrying serially.

Same-machine comparisons copy only the benchmark harness to the base checkout. Base and head each build worker payloads from their own algorithms; the base must support #3125's runtime.

Validation: six focused tests / 131 assertions, including native Bun threaded output/statistics/iteration parity and cleanup after an exception; package build and declarations pass. Local full TypeScript check has the same 67 pre-existing diagnostics as baseline. No performance benchmark was run.

title: Speed up Pipeline9 joint DRC repair with an early bounded pass
description: Run bounded regional repair before the broad exactB01 portfolio on boards without preloaded copper, achieving a 3.96 local speedup while maintaining zero-issue reference DRC results.
body:
Run bounded regional repair before the broad exact/B01 portfolio on boards without preloaded copper. A candidate may finish the joint solver only after whole-board reference DRC reports zero issues; incomplete candidates remain private and the existing stages receive their original geometry. Preloaded boards retain their existing stage order, and all work still advances synchronously through `.step()`.

On the supplied 244-route debugger export, three fresh-process runs per revision (alternating order, including construction) gave:

| | Baseline main | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median time | 28.661 s | 7.242 s |
| Individual runs | 25.428, 28.661, 30.878 s | 7.169, 7.242, 9.098 s |
| Final reference DRC issues | 0 | 0 |
| Routes | 244 | 244 |
| Vias | 542 | 548 |
| Wire length | 4754.655 mm | 4771.252 mm |

This is a **3.96× local speedup**. Equivalence here means the same connection endpoints and zero-issue reference DRC result; geometry is different: six additional vias and 0.35% additional wire. All terminal positions, connection identities, trace widths and via diameters are preserved. All three optimized runs produced the same output SHA-256, `9431397b5602545691a8da26e78f1c713dc9680b41faffef6e4b0578e8d90536`.

Validation:
- 25 relevant tests passed, including independent reference DRC and repeated solve/step determinism on the supplied input.
- Mandatory synthetic tests cover early completion, one-step child advancement, unchanged terminals, incomplete-candidate isolation, preload ownership, budgets and later-stage failure propagation.
- Current-dependency validation uses `@tscircuit/checks` 0.0.255 for both revisions. The supplied-input regression passes 26,206 assertions, including independent reference DRC and solve/step determinism. Output hashes are unchanged from the earlier dependency installation.
- All nine GitHub Actions test shards pass on `e781a42` ([test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/39006956946)). Type checking, both CI builds, formatting, repository policy checks and Vercel deployment also pass.
- The existing sample 2 limit of 510 vias is preserved by a second cleanup sweep when early repair introduces vias. Updated routing snapshots have been reviewed; incomplete candidates still cannot be published. Early completion reports both its bounded work counters and matching budget limits.
- Source baseline: `9d95bfdde15f739bdb362d38a01f7f6ac2c63450`. Runtime: Bun 1.3.2, macOS ARM64. Three fresh processes per revision ran in alternating order using the same installed dependencies.

The supplied board input is intentionally excluded from the public repository. To reproduce with a local debugger export:

```sh
bun scripts/benchmarkPipeline9JointDrcInput.ts /path/to/input.json
PIPELINE9_JOINT_DRC_INPUT=/path/to/input.json bun test tests/repro/pipeline9-joint-drc-input.test.ts --timeout 9999999
```

The benchmark accepts `JOINT_DRC_SOLVER_MODULE` pointing to an absolute baseline solver module path for revision comparisons.

title: repro: circular holes are only half cut in STEP exports

body:
A circular `pcb_hole` comes out of the STEP export only partly cut, with material
left standing inside the hole.

The fixture is `sample014-usb-c-power-adapter` from the circuit json
dataset: a 21.9 x 52.5 mm board with seven circular holes between 0.65 mm and
2.2 mm, four of them `pcb_hole` and three `pcb_plated_hole`.

A ray dropped straight down through the centre of a hole should cross no
triangles, because the hole is open edge to edge. Each of these crosses once or
twice, which is material standing inside the hole.

| probe | crossings |
| --- | --- |
| centre of the 2.2 mm plated hole | 1 |
| centre of the other 6 holes | 2 |
| board material at (6.1, 0.4) | 2 |
| board material at (0.2, -8.7) | 2 |

The defect is confined to the inside of a circular hole, and it affects
plated and non-plated holes alike.

body:
Solvers can now register their constructors once and execute by name through an inline runtime or a reusable Bun/Node worker pool. The same registration supplies the serial implementation; callers do not pass a separate fallback function.

```ts
class HighDensityNodeSolver extends BaseSolver {
  static readonly solverName: string = "HighDensityNodeSolver"
  // Existing solver implementation...
}
SolverRuntime.registerSolver(HighDensityNodeSolver)

// Both forms use the same registration and worker selection.
const byName = await runtime.executeAsync("HighDensityNodeSolver", params)
const byClass = await runtime.executeAsync(HighDensityNodeSolver, params)
```

Every registered class must define its own non-empty static `solverName`, including subclasses; runtime validation rejects inherited/missing/invalid names and conflicting registrations. Class calls infer constructor input and `getOutput()` types. Constructors are never sent through worker messages, and class invocation does not auto-register.

Each request constructs the registered solver, awaits `solveAsync(runtime)` when implemented (otherwise calls synchronous `solve()`), rejects reported failure, and returns `getOutput()`. Existing BaseSolver, stepping, and synchronous solving are unchanged.

### Parallel orchestration

Keep the parent on the host and let its async method submit child solvers:

```ts
async solveAsync(runtime: SolverRuntimeExecutor): Promise<void> {
  const pending = this.nodeInputs.map(input =>
    runtime.executeAsync(HighDensityNodeSolver, input),
  )
  const outputs = await Promise.all(pending)
  for (const output of outputs) this.applyOutput(output)
  this.solved = true
}

// Host
const parent = new HighDensityPhaseSolver(input)
await parent.solveAsync(runtime)
```

A parent submitted as a worker task also works, but descendants execute inline inside that worker. This initial policy prevents nested pools and starvation; host orchestration is necessary to parallelize children. Solvers still own deterministic commits, seeds, iteration budgets, and cache behavior.

### Registration and packaging

- Default `@tscircuit/solver-utils` entry exports the inline runtime and typed executor/transport contracts, without Node worker imports.
- Optional `/runtime/bun` and `/runtime/node` entries share the default registry. Prefer the native Bun adapter on Bun.
- Worker entrypoints import their solver registration modules, then call `SolverRuntime.listen()`. Registration in the parent does not install worker code.
- Hosts build those entrypoints into self-contained source strings: ESM/Blob workers on Bun, CommonJS/eval workers on Node. No adjacent worker path is required after rebundling. An explicit `workerUrl` option also supports unbundled applications.
- Inputs/outputs have native message-clone isolation in both modes, preserving intentional SharedArrayBuffer sharing.
- [docs/solver-runtime.md](https://github.com/tscircuit/solver-utils/blob/feat/solver-runtime/docs/solver-runtime.md) includes complete examples and the worker-source generation step.

### Execution selection and lifecycle

Workers advertise registrations during startup. Missing worker registration uses the local registered constructor; unknown names reject. Startup errors throw by default, with an opt-in diagnosed `startupFailure: "serial"` policy. `requireWorker: true` disables serial execution for CI and parity checks. Slow tasks never trigger serial retries.

Solver exceptions reject without retries; unexpected worker exits reject outstanding/future work. Disposal rejects pending work and terminates owned workers, including partially initialized pools. Inline synchronous work is not interruptible; per-task progress/cancellation is outside this initial API.

Threaded execution under Bun requires 1.4.2+ after observing worker-cleanup hangs/crashes on 1.3.2. Tested locally with the available Bun 1.4.2; downloading latest stable 1.4.3 was blocked by network access. The existing structural SolverExecutor contract remains unchanged. Downstream autorouter/core/eval/CLI adoption is separate.

### Validation

- 33 tests / 184 assertions pass on Bun 1.4.2, including real concurrent leaf tasks, serial/async parity, nested dispatch, missing registrations, startup/partial startup failure, shared memory, failed solver states, worker exits, and disposal.
- Type checking, package build/declarations, and repository format check pass.
- Minified packed tarball checks exercise both class and string invocation and pass on actual Node 26.4.0 and Bun 1.4.2, with externalized and fully rebundled consumers; tests require remote execution, exercise async orchestration and local registration sharing, and verify errors.
- Packed browser bundle runs inline without Node worker imports.
- CI now builds and runs the packed consumer checks with Node 22 and latest Bun.

The isolated packaging check bundles the real installed graphics-debug peer/dependencies rather than performing a network install; it tests solver-utils' package boundary.

title: Add typed solver executor and shared-memory contracts
description: Add a typed solver executor and shared-memory contracts to enable solvers to share execution resources without depending on a parent autorouter.
body:
Solvers need a common execution contract so hypergraph, high-density, repair, and other packages can share one host-owned executor without depending on a parent autorouter.

- Add `SolverExecutor<Tasks>`, typed task catalogs/context, and `SolverSharedMemory` through the existing public entrypoint. Task kinds determine input, result, and shared-context types; a combined executor can serve smaller catalogs.
- Add `createSharedSolverBuffer(view)` to copy exactly a typed array or DataView's visible bytes into a fixed shared allocation. Related tasks can reuse the backing storage without copying topology per worker.
- Document immutable shared inputs, task-owned mutable state, host disposal, structured-clone isolation, and serial-order consumption. Seeds, cache visibility, logical budgets, and candidate selection remain solver responsibilities.
- Keep `BaseSolver` and `BasePipelineSolver` unchanged. No task dispatch or worker pool is enabled by this PR.

Validation passes locally:
- All 24 tests, 99 assertions, including native-worker shared storage/publication and byte-exact snapshot isolation.
- Full TypeScript check, including invalid task/input/result/shared-context calls and combined-catalog reuse.
- Repository formatting check.
- Both package entrypoint builds with declaration generation.
- Smoke import of the helper from built `dist/index.js`.

Local dependencies were restored from the Bun cache; validation used symlink-preservation flags for that checkout.

This replaces the generic implementation proposed in https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3109. The autorouter integration can consume this package after release.

title: Add opt-in KiCad schematic electrical grid alignment (#283)
description: Adds opt-in electrical grid alignment for KiCad schematics, allowing users to align electrical connections with a specified grid size while preserving existing coordinates and designs.
body:
This stacked fix is merged into #667. **Review the complete change in [#667](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/pull/667), which targets `main`.**

Adds opt-in electrical grid alignment for #283. Pass `schematicGridSize` in KiCad millimeters, e.g. `0.25` or `1.27` (50 mil). Default exports retain their current coordinates; this avoids changing existing and imported designs.

The final sheet pass aligns symbol origins, global pin positions, wire vertices, junctions and label anchors together. Library definitions are cloned per instance because a shared symbol may need different local pin offsets at different page positions. Generated names reserve all existing library IDs. Native artwork primitives are preserved, reference fields move with their symbol, and the input Circuit JSON is unchanged. An overly coarse grid that would merge distinct pins is rejected. Both standalone and hierarchical sheet paths apply the option.

This is independent of #292's default-coordinate precision issue and existing PR #347. It does not replace the custom-symbol geometry fix in #664.

Validation:
- Four ordinary regressions fail on unchanged main and pass with the fix (154 assertions).
- KiCad 10.0.1 XML netlists confirm L1.2/R1.1/R3.1 share their labeled net and L2.2/R2.1 share their separate net, on both 0.25 mm and 50 mil grids.
- Native PNG snapshot rendered with the existing helper and visually inspected.
- Full TypeScript check, package/declaration build, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Existing CI workflows and coverage are unchanged. Reviewed Seve's #467/#474/#478 feedback and core#2607/#3208: no authored Circuit JSON, source-port compensation, or conversion of native artwork primitives into replacement shapes.

![Grid-aligned native KiCad export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/fix/schematic-grid/tests/sch/repros/__snapshots__/repro283-schematic-grid.snap.png)



Local default-export controls: 1 pass / 7 snapshot mismatches; the same seven failures and exact mismatch percentages reproduce on unchanged main in this environment. The generated fixture also exports byte-identically with the option omitted, apart from generated UUIDs, before and after the change.

title: Fix standalone KiCad converter package dependencies
description: Fixes dependency issues in the standalone KiCad converter package by declaring runtime packages as peers and ensuring proper imports for isolated production consumers.
body:
This stacked fix is merged into #665. **Review the complete change in [#665](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/pull/665), which targets `main`.**

A standalone install could not import `circuit-json-to-kicad`: its build leaves runtime imports external, but the package declared only a TypeScript peer. Declare those runtime packages and the public `circuit-json` type dependency as peers, with explicit development dependencies for the two imports previously supplied transitively. Keep the original `tsup-node lib/index.ts --format esm --dts` build command. No bundling config, converter logic, snapshots, or CI changes.

Use published `kicadts@^0.0.58` as the runtime peer. The existing Git development pin came from merged #495 to support EBAZ legacy-file tests. Its source branch belongs to [kicadts#68](https://github.com/tscircuit/kicadts/pull/68), which was closed without merging; the published parser still rejects that legacy metadata. Preserve the existing dev pin for those tests while standalone consumers use the normal prebuilt npm release. This removes the special `kicadts` JavaScript/type bundling and declaration-path overrides from the earlier implementation.

Validation: the ordinary packed-consumer test fails on the repro branch with missing `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util`. With this fix, an isolated production consumer installs the tarball and published peers, checks consumer types, imports the converter, and produces schematic output. It also verifies that `getOutput()` returns an instance of the peer's `KicadSch` class. Build, full repository TypeScript check, formatting, and diff checks pass.

The dev/peer arrangement follows [Seve's merged peer-dependency review](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/pull/43#discussion_r2701297550). Shared Circuit JSON peers use `*`. Related closed/merged reviews #467, #474, #596, #623 and the existing Git-pin history in #495 were checked. Existing tests and CI coverage remain enabled.

title: Fix default layers blocking native AM3352 DDR escapes
