title: Reduce temporary allocations while parsing and writing STEP files
description: Reduces memory usage and export time by parsing one entity at a time and writing STEP text in batches, optimizing the handling of large STEP files.
body:
Large STEP exports retain every raw statement and token row during parsing, then allocate repository-entry tuples and a complete array of entity strings during serialization.

Parse one entity at a time internally, slice source spans instead of building statements character by character, and write STEP text in batches of 1,024 lines. Keep `tokenizeSTEP()` returning an array and `toPartFile()` returning one string, with the same syntax validation, entity order and emitted bytes. No dependencies or regex rewrites are added.

For `imrishabh18/corne-keyboard@2.0.33`, three independent Bun 1.3.14 processes per variant give these medians:

| Changes | Export time | Peak process RSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published converter/stepts baseline | 5.10 s | 1.94 GB |
| This PR alone | 4.83 s | 1.83 GB |
| This PR + [converter optimization](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/pull/163) | 2.29 s | 1.56 GB |

The combined result uses about 20% less peak memory and takes about 55% less time. These are cached-asset Bun measurements, including conversion, Blob creation and a local file write; they exclude network transfer and are not browser-memory measurements. Peak memory remains substantial. Every variant produces a byte-identical 79,499,896-byte STEP file.

Validation:
- 31 stepts tests pass, including existing visual snapshots and SolidWorks/KiCad round trips.
- Extend the 150,000-entity test to serialize and parse all entities, preserving IDs and values; cover adjacent comments, Unicode names and malformed input through the incremental parser.
- The converter's 46 tests also pass against this change.
- Native Open CASCADE imports all 549 solids and 93,160 faces from the optimized Corne assembly without load-check errors.
- Build, TypeScript, formatting and whitespace checks pass.

title: fix: use npm trusted publishing for releases
description: Fixes npm publishing process by enabling trusted publishing and adding controlled recovery for failed releases.
body:
The failed release used Node 20/npm 10.8.2 with a stored token and no OIDC permission. This change enables npm trusted publishing and adds a controlled recovery for the tag that was pushed before npm failed.

## Behavior

- Use Node 24 and npm 11 (>=11.5.1), grant publishing jobs `id-token: write`, and remove the publish step's `NPM_TOKEN` mapping. Stored secrets and 2FA settings are untouched. Update setup-node/create-pull-request to versions with supported action runtimes.
- Ignore `.github/**`-only pushes. **All files in this PR are under `.github/`, so merging this PR by itself cannot publish**, regardless of merge title or strategy. Do not combine unrelated source changes into the migration merge.
- Ordinary main-branch source changes still run the existing Bun build/pver release/version-bump PR flow. Guard both squash and merge commits for `chore: bump version to ...` and legacy `vX.Y.Z` commits so bot auto-merges do not start another release.
- Manual dispatch defaults to `none`. A routine manual release requires operation `release` and confirmation `release next version`. Only main can publish.
- Serialize release/recovery runs with `npm-release` concurrency and do not cancel an active publication.

## Narrow recovery operation

In this same trusted workflow filename, `recover-0.0.5` requires confirmation `publish stepts@0.0.5` and branch main. Its separate job:

1. Checks out exactly `f159444d7615ccabdfd53a7c8b06f9688675e577`, verifies HEAD and remote tag `v0.0.5`, and checks package identity `stepts@0.0.5`.
2. Installs frozen dependencies, builds, and runs tests.
3. Fetches public npm metadata immediately before publication; fails closed on HTTP/network/JSON errors, an existing 0.0.5, unexpected package metadata, or latest no longer being 0.0.4.
4. Runs `npm publish` once. It does not run pver, push tags, create a version-bump PR, or enable auto-merge. It has no bot token and disables checkout credential persistence.

Rerunning recovery after successful publication fails the existing-version check. A concurrent external publisher can still win the registry race; npm's immutable version handling then rejects the duplicate.

## Validation (no publication)

- Node 24.19.0 / npm 11.21.1 / Bun 1.4.3: frozen install, build, npm pack --dry-run, 30 library tests (161 assertions), typecheck and format check passed.
- 25 committed Node tests exercise push, legacy/squash/merge bump messages, deleted/missing refs, PRs, all dispatch operations/confirmations/branches, and registry-state validation. The PR test workflow runs these tests.
- Mocked recovery shell execution passed for valid source, wrong HEAD, moved/missing tag, wrong package/version, already-published version, changed latest, invalid JSON and HTTP/network failure. Only the valid case invoked a mocked npm publish; no real publish command ran.
- YAML parsing, actionlint 1.7.7, and git diff --check passed. Verified the migration touches only ignored paths and dispatch defaults to none.
- Packaging and mocked tests do not prove npm's live OIDC trust; that is validated only by an approved publication.

## npm setup — separate approval still required

Package **stepts** → Settings → Trusted publishing → GitHub Actions:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Organization/user | `tscircuit` |
| Repository | `stepts` |
| Workflow filename | `bun-pver-release.yml` |
| Environment | blank |
| Direct npm publish | enabled |
| Separate npm dist-tag permission | off |

Keep 2FA enabled. No change to Rishabh's or anyone else's npm account permissions is needed or included. New trust must complete its first successful publish within two days; coordinate configuration with recovery approval.

References: [npm trusted publishing requirements and settings](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/), [GitHub OIDC permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/security-harden-deployments/oidc-in-cloud-providers).

## Observed failure and remaining uncertainty

[Failed job](https://github.com/tscircuit/stepts/actions/runs/39158824935/job/117767580849) returned `E404` for npm PUT, not an explicit 2FA error. The precise old-token failure is unknown. The obsolete npm and absent OIDC permission are confirmed trusted-publishing blockers. Separate npm browser inspection confirmed no trusted publisher was configured.

Read-only registry check on 2026-10-19: versions 0.0.1–0.0.4, latest 0.0.4. Tag v0.0.5 already points to the pinned commit above. Main's package version remains 0.0.2. The failed run did not reach bump-PR creation. Older bump PRs #17 (0.0.3) and #19 (0.0.4) are open without auto-merge. A normal pver release would currently skip v0.0.5 and choose 0.0.6.

## Exact approved recovery sequence

1. Review passing checks and approve merging this PR alone. Its workflow-only path filter prevents a migration release. Do not re-run the old failed job.
2. Separately approve and configure the npm trust fields above. Coordinate recovery before other source changes reach main; ordinary source pushes remain automatic releases.
3. After confirming main contains this reviewed change and the tag/registry state remains as documented, separately approve **one publication of stepts@0.0.5 to npm with latest/provenance, using the pinned source and no tag pushes, bump PR or auto-merge**. Run:

   ```sh
   gh workflow run bun-pver-release.yml --repo tscircuit/stepts --ref main \
     -f operation=recover-0.0.5 \
     -f confirmation='publish stepts@0.0.5'
   ```

4. Verify the run, registry version/latest and provenance. Reconcile main's package version and stale bump PRs separately; do not merge the stale 0.0.3/0.0.4 bump PRs as recovery. A reconciliation PR named `chore: bump version to 0.0.5` is skipped by the release guard for either squash or merge commit, and needs its own merge approval.

No live npm settings, publication, merge, dispatch, auto-merge setting, stored secret, or account permission has been changed as part of preparing this PR. No disable/re-enable workflow procedure is required.

title: Fix STEP tokenization and preserve imported geometry types
description: Fixes tokenization issues in STEP files with whitespace before semicolons and preserves the integrity of imported geometry types by ensuring 2D geometry is treated separately from 3D geometry, along with proper serialization of spline multiplicities and logical values.
body:
Valid STEP files with whitespace before semicolons fail tokenization, and reserializing imported geometry can change its meaning: 2D UV coordinates gain a Z coordinate, spline integer multiplicities become real numbers, and logical `.U.` becomes `.F.`. JavaScript scientific notation also produces invalid STEP real literals.

Parse statements and arguments with one scanner that respects strings, doubled quotes, comments and nested lists. Entity delimiters inside strings or comments no longer split records. Accept whitespace around entity terminators directly, without rewriting the input.

Preserve 2D geometry as `CartesianPoint2D` and `Direction2D`, separate from existing 3D classes so model-space transforms do not modify UV coordinates. Serialize spline multiplicities as integers and retain unknown logicals as `null` / `.U.`. Format real mantissas and uppercase exponents in `fmtNum`, where number types are known.

Validation:
- All 30 tests pass, along with TypeScript, formatting, whitespace checks and ESM/declaration build.
- Regressions cover delimiters in strings/comments, escaped quotes, multiline strings, malformed syntax, 2D and 3D entities, spline round-trips, exponent formatting, non-finite numbers and labels containing `1e-10`.
- The SolidWorks-format fixture round-trips through Open CASCADE with identical vertex and index arrays and a checked-in visual snapshot.
- A local integration with the cleaned converter exports the Corne package in about 7 seconds with all 165 assembly children. Native Open CASCADE reads it without load-check errors and transfers all 549 solids (93,160 faces).

![SolidWorks-format STEP round-trip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/stepts/3e11a25421c898cee401d038b0a889c3130ff761/tests/roundtrip/solidworks/__snapshots__/solidworks-roundtrip.snap.png)

Moves parser compatibility fixes out of https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/pull/145. After this is merged and published, a converter dependency update can also remove its pre-existing exponent postprocessing.

title: feat: detect inductors separated from their connected chip pin pair
description: Detects inductors that are placed away from their connected chip pin pairs, ensuring proper schematic representation and connectivity.
body:
L1 is drawn above U2 while its two private connections go to pins on the chip's right side. `ChipPinPairInductorPlacementSolver` reports `InductorSeparatedFromChipPins` for an inductor placed far from two exclusively connected pins on the same side of one chip. The existing `ChipSupplyInductorPlacementSolver` requires one explicit power-rail end, so it does not cover this topology.

Stack: **#309 (TSX repro) → this PR (analyzer and correction)**. Merge #309 first. This stack is independent of the fuse/diode stack #308 → #310.

![Chip and inductor before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/1828a151df6cdf1a53e2895d76556518a9084fbf/tests/cases/__snapshots__/chip-pin-pair-inductor-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

This is a hand-arranged TSX correction, not an automatic move produced by the analyzer. It moves L1 beside the two pins and rotates it to keep both wires visible. U2's symbol and pin layout stay unchanged. The focused comparison omits other chip boundary connections equally in both panels and uses equal scale, a divider, red markers and red diagnostics. The [complete original seven-part regulator section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/1828a151df6cdf1a53e2895d76556518a9084fbf/tests/cases/__snapshots__/remote-chip-pin-inductor-repro-full.snap.svg) remains available with the new finding highlighted.

The [complete corrected regulator section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/1828a151df6cdf1a53e2895d76556518a9084fbf/tests/cases/__snapshots__/chip-pin-pair-inductor-correction-full-section.snap.svg) has **zero findings from full placement analysis**, with all seven components and electrical connections preserved. R5/R6 also move into a compact feedback branch to resolve the rail-path finding exposed by rerouting L1. This zero-findings claim covers the regulator section, not the other sheets of the published remote.

Detection requires a typed `simple_inductor`, two distinct private two-port nets, one typed chip, two pins on the same drawing side and unambiguous geometry in the same local scope. Explicit power/ground/voltage roles, fanout, different chips/scopes, overlaps, missing/duplicate geometry and unpopulated/disconnected parts are excluded. There are no semantic checks of names, pin hints, net labels or reference designators. Missing supply flags are not proof of a switching role: the rule makes only a connectivity and schematic-placement claim. Its distance allowance scales with symbol size and pin spacing; exact alignment is not required.

Source: [AnasSarkiz/tscircuit-ai-agent-remote v0.0.11-wip-generator-qualification](https://tscircuit.com/AnasSarkiz/tscircuit-ai-agent-remote?version=0.0.11-wip-generator-qualification#schematic). [TI TPS63802, Typical Application on page 1](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps63802.pdf#page=1) draws the inductor beside its two connected pins. TI's pins face upward; this imported chip's pins face right, so the corrected inductor orientation differs. The numerical distance threshold is a readability heuristic, not a TI electrical requirement.

**Existing snapshot impact:** the drone fixture also has L1 on the opposite side of its two connected U3 pins. Its original full-sheet snapshot gains this real finding (8 → 9). Its corrected full-sheet snapshot moves/rotates L1 beside those pins and remains at zero findings. Tests verify both inductor wires remain visibly continuous and all source connectivity is unchanged. The motor comparison/detail snapshots do not change. No dependency or schema changes are included.

Validation: full `bun test` **254 passed**; typecheck, formatting and browser build passed. Guard tests cover renamed labels, rotations/reflections, thresholds, typed rails, ambiguous topology and incomplete records. The comparison reuses the existing schematic background fill.

title: feat: detect misaligned fuse and diode series paths
description: Detects misaligned fuse and diode series paths in schematics and reports alignment issues without automatic corrections.
body:
A fuse and diode with one private shared junction can still be drawn on different axes, hiding their simple series path. `FuseDiodeAlignmentSolver` reports `FuseDiodeNotAligned` when their connected schematic pins are staggered, perpendicular or face away from each other.

Stack: **#308 (TSX repro) → this PR (analyzer and correction)**. Merge #308 first. This stack is independent of the chip pin-pair inductor stack #309 → #311.

![Fuse and diode before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/6348ed8680a629ae5b0e6f5f6977fd6d09623527/tests/cases/__snapshots__/fuse-diode-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The hand-arranged TSX pair correction rotates the fuse and shifts it 0.04 mm to align the native symbol terminals. In the complete filtering section, it also rotates D_MOTOR_TVS by 180° so its ground-connected anode faces down and its cathode connects above. Diode polarity and every electrical connection are preserved. The analyzer reports the issue; it does not automatically apply this correction. The comparison uses the same scale, a divider, red numbered markers and red diagnostics. The [original filtering section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/6348ed8680a629ae5b0e6f5f6977fd6d09623527/tests/cases/__snapshots__/astra-fuse-diode-repro-filter.snap.svg) now highlights the finding, and the [corrected complete five-component filtering section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/6348ed8680a629ae5b0e6f5f6977fd6d09623527/tests/cases/__snapshots__/fuse-diode-correction-full-section.snap.svg) has **zero findings from full placement analysis**. That claim applies to this extracted section, not the rest of the published motor board.

The original D_MOTOR_TVS orientation is not currently reported: the existing inverted-rail check requires explicit positive-supply metadata, while VMOTOR_PROTECTED is only a display label in this extract. Its visual correction is included in the TSX example; this PR does not add a ground-above detection rule or invent supply metadata. The correction test checks the ground symbol below the diode, the continuous cathode wire, and unchanged electrical records.

Detection uses `simple_fuse`, `simple_diode`, connectivity, unique local placements and schematic pin geometry. Both parts must have two distinct terminal nets and share exactly one private two-port junction. It accepts horizontal or vertical paths with a small alignment tolerance. Parallel pairs, junction fanout, different local scopes, overlaps, missing/duplicate geometry and unpopulated/disconnected parts are skipped. Names and labels are used only in diagnostic text, never to infer electrical roles.

Source: [Astra motor controller v1.4.0](https://tscircuit.com/astra/nema17-stepper-motor-controller-spring-clamp-rp2040?version=1.4.0#schematic). [TI DM388 Base Board, Figure A-36 “PowerIn”, page 109](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/sprui85/sprui85.pdf#page=109) shows a fuse and series diode on a straight horizontal supply path. This supports the drawing convention; it does not specify a numeric schematic spacing requirement.

Validation: the full suite passed **251 tests**, plus typecheck, formatting and browser build. Tests verify unchanged electrical records, visible wire continuity, arbitrary renamed labels, rotated/reflected geometry, tolerance boundaries and insufficient evidence. Only this repro's snapshots change; no dependencies change. The comparison reuses the existing background fill so equal-scale camera margins match the schematic.

The correction is a hand-arranged TSX example, not an automatic move produced by the analyzer. It groups the series resistor/capacitor beside the parallel capacitor, preserving all values, symbols and pin connections. The test verifies unchanged electrical records, the resistor's rotation, and continuous drawn wires for all three nodes.

Detection uses typed resistors/capacitors and connectivity: a private two-terminal R–C junction, distinct outer nodes, and exactly one additional capacitor across those outer nodes. It reports shared-pin distance above `max(4, 3 × largest R/C symbol dimension)` in schematic units. This is a readability allowance, not an electrical constraint or a demand for exact alignment. No name/label/hint checks or inference that the network is a compensation circuit are used. Ambiguous capacitor banks, branched/rail junctions, rail-only outer nodes, different scopes, missing/duplicate geometry, invalid passive values, overlaps and unpopulated/disconnected parts are skipped.

Source: [0hmX/dual-usb-peltier-assembly v0.4.3](https://tscircuit.com/0hmX/dual-usb-peltier-assembly?version=0.4.3#schematic). The result applies to the complete **three-component extract**, not the regulator or the full POWER sheet. The author's v0.4.8 placement already groups these parts and is included as a passing guard case. [TI TPS55289, Figure 8-1, page 33](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55289.pdf#page=33) shows R3/C6 together beside C7; reference values are not substituted into the repro.

Validation: `bun test` (248 tests), typecheck, formatting and browser build. Guards cover renamed labels, orientation/translation, ambiguous topology and incomplete records. Published positions, symbols, values and connectivity were independently checked against the original export. No dependencies or unrelated snapshots change. The comparison reuses the viewport background fill already merged in #303.

title: feat: detect crossed parallel diode connections
description: Detects and reports crossed parallel diode connections where two diodes share the same nets but are drawn at opposite ends, preventing wraparound wires.
body:
D4/D5 share both nets but draw the matching net ends on opposite sides, producing wraparound wires. `ParallelDiodeAlignmentSolver` reports `ParallelDiodesNotAligned` for this local pair. The existing shared-node diode rule excludes pairs sharing both nets, so it does not cover this case.

Stack: **#302 (TSX repro) → this PR (analyzer and correction)**. Merge #302 first. This stack is independent of the series-RC-branch stack #304 → #305.

![Complete diode pair before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/42543cd70d8b21136e3706d59579acf036816c5d/tests/cases/__snapshots__/parallel-diode-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The comparison uses equal scale, a divider, red numbered markers and red diagnostics. The [original repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/42543cd70d8b21136e3706d59579acf036816c5d/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pir-parallel-diodes-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) now highlights the new finding. The [corrected complete extract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/42543cd70d8b21136e3706d59579acf036816c5d/tests/cases/__snapshots__/parallel-diode-correction-full-sheet.snap.svg) has **zero findings from full placement analysis**.

The correction is a hand-arranged TSX example, not an automatic move produced by the analyzer. It rotates D4 by 180 degrees and brings it closer to D5, preserving component metadata, symbol family and every electrical connection. Both shared nets have verified continuous drawn wires.

Detection requires exactly two typed diodes across the same two distinct nets, in the same local scope. It orders their schematic pins by electrical net identity and reports opposite endpoint order on the same drawing axis. It makes no semantic checks of names, labels or hints, and does not infer anode/cathode roles. Larger banks, rail-only pairs, remote blocks, overlaps, missing/duplicate placements or ports, invalid geometry and unpopulated/disconnected parts are skipped. This rule addresses crossed endpoint order; it does not prescribe an exact gap or diagnose arbitrary diode arrangements.

Source: [abse/boostxl-tlv8544pir v1.0.21](https://tscircuit.com/abse/boostxl-tlv8544pir?version=1.0.21#schematic). The zero-findings result applies to the complete **two-diode extract**, not the other amplifier components or full published board. [TI TIDA-00489, Figure 27, page 22](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/snou148a/snou148a.pdf#page=22) shows D4/D5 between the same two buses.

Validation: `bun test` (245 tests), typecheck, formatting and browser build. Add IBIS model/pin bindings, per-experiment pin states, binary traffic, and probe-bound eye requests to the public Circuit JSON union.

Models reference an IBIS file through the shared Asset schema in ibis_model_asset. Explicit fields identify the vendor [Component], map IBIS [Pin] names to source_port_id values and selected [Model] names, and identify each supply/clamp reference port. model_value_corner selects the vendor typ/min/max data column; include_package_parasitics controls package R/L/C. title: Preserve board via-in-pad policy through SRJ routing
description: Fixes the omission of the via-in-pad policy during SRJ conversion, ensuring that the routing input retains the boards permission for vias in pads.
body:
**Motivation:** Boards that permit vias in pads must retain that permission in the actual routing input. PMP22650's imported board record explicitly enables it.

**Actual:** Circuit JSON contains `is_via_in_pad_allowed: true`, but SRJ conversion omits `allowViaInPad`. Even after copying the policy into SRJ, local routing and the simplified remote path discard it by assigning an unspecified autorouter option.

**Expected / fix:** Copy the selected board's policy into SRJ, defaulting an absent policy to `false`. At both local and simplified remote routing handoffs, use the autorouter option only when it is specified. Explicit `false` and `true` overrides retain precedence.

The change stays in the existing conversion function and the two existing assignments in `Group.ts`; it adds no dependency or abstraction. All new tests and fixtures live in the base reproduction PR. This PR updates direct assertions, the single combined PCB/policy SVG snapshot, and the existing full-SRJ inline snapshot: the local callback and remote HTTP payload now receive `true`, while explicit-disable controls still receive `false`.

The single combined snapshot shows the emitted policy values below the illustrative **2.74 × 2.74 mm exposed GND pad with four manually placed blind thermal vias**, spanning `top` to `inner1`. The handoff tests inspect a small board's actual callback input and HTTP payload; they do not claim full-board routing completion.

**Validation:**

- 66 focused tests across 61 files pass, covering SRJ conversion, imported policies, owning-board selection, local and remote handoffs, explicit overrides, and routing phases.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 bunx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 bun run build` passes, including ESM and TypeScript declarations.
- The combined PCB/policy snapshot was visually checked; `git diff --check` passes.

**Related:** Stacked on the passing reproduction in [core #4688](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4688). Merge the reproduction first, then retarget this PR to `main`. Dataset regeneration can consume the released core fix afterward.

title: Reproduce dropped board via-in-pad policy in routing input
description: Reproduces the issue of dropped board via-in-pad policy in routing input, ensuring that the boards via-in-pad permission is preserved during routing processes.
body:
**Motivation:** Keep a board's via-in-pad permission when preparing routing input. PMP22650 in dataset-srj24 explicitly allows vias in pads.

**Actual:** `getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson` omits `pcb_board.is_via_in_pad_allowed`. Local routing and the simplified remote endpoint also overwrite the SRJ permission with an unspecified autorouter option. The local callback receives `undefined`; the HTTP request omits the flag.

This passing reproduction captures the current output in separate tests with direct assertions for imported policies (`true`, `false`, and unspecified), local routing, and remote routing. Separate local and remote control tests verify that an explicit `allowViaInPad: false` takes precedence. The existing owning-board test covers a nested subcircuit in a panel.

The sole added visual snapshot combines the emitted policy values with a PCB view of a **2.74 × 2.74 mm exposed GND pad with four manually placed thermal vias**, spanning `top` to `inner1` (0.61 mm outer diameter, 0.30 mm hole). Routing handoff tests use a small board with one connection and inspect the actual callback input or localhost HTTP payload; their stub routers return no traces.

**Expected:** Preserve the selected board's policy in SRJ and through routing unless the autorouter explicitly overrides it. An unspecified board policy should remain disabled. This PR contains reproduction coverage only; current buggy outputs are asserted so tests pass.

**Validation:** Eight focused tests pass, repository-wide TypeScript checking passes with a 4 GiB Node heap, and the combined PCB/policy snapshot was visually checked. Each new scenario has its own test file.

**Related:** The source fixture is the unmodified `pcb_board` record from [dataset-srj24 sample024 at 004847d1](https://github.com/tscircuit/dataset-srj24/blob/004847d1fc526330f1d8f1b3abe5c8ed65d161b4/circuit-json/sample024-pmp22650-main.json). The fix is stacked in [core #4689](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4689).

title: perf: resolve trace names only for diagnostics
description: Optimizes trace-continuity validation by resolving readable names for PCB traces only when emitting diagnostics, reducing unnecessary naming work and preserving existing behavior for connectivity and geometry checks.
body:
Trace-continuity validation resolves readable names for every PCB trace, including successful checks and fragments skipped because their source trace was already checked. Source-trace naming also visits every connected port even though its label displays at most two readable names.

Resolve each trace name only when emitting a diagnostic, and stop source-port lookup after the first two readable names. Preserve first-match lookup behavior, duplicate names, fallback labels, error text, and ordering. Connectivity and geometry checks retain their existing behavior.

Validation:
- Full CI is green on `506f9e0`, including formatting, type checking, tests, builds, dependency checks, and both packed-consumer variants.
- Focused tests cover zero naming calls for valid fragmented nets, exact named/unnamed diagnostics, duplicate-record first-match behavior, display-name priority, and bounded lookup work on long port lists.
- Independent source review found no semantic change beyond avoiding unused naming work.

The official [CI-built preview](https://pkg.pr.new/@tscircuit/checks@506f9e0) is consumed by [autorouter PR #3139](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139), head `9992658`. All seven consumer benchmark pairs completed after that PR's full CI passed. Pipeline 9, effort 1, concurrency 4, Bun 1.4.2, eight logical ARM64 CPUs, and fresh per-board processes were fixed.

| SRJ18 pair | Joint DRC time | Total stage time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275185028) | −13.28% | −3.78% |
| [2](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275296473) | −13.09% | −5.43% |
| [3](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275298764) | −10.05% | −1.97% |

Combined joint DRC time falls 12.19%, accounting for 87.8% of net recorded stage savings; high-density routing is flat across these runs. The consumer also contains an exact A13 ownership optimization, so the complete consumer speedup is not attributed solely to this dependency.

[Artifact verification](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/39314701247) covers all three dataset 1 pairs, three SRJ18 pairs, and one SRJ24 pair: 329 paired records covering 127 unique inputs and 321 byte-identical SVG pairs. Routing, DRC messages, via counts, lint counts, and search metrics match. Seven pre-existing SRJ24 timeout error strings differ only in recorded numeric progress observations; those differences were preserved separately. No whole-record exactness is claimed for those timeout strings.

The consumer base uses checks 0.0.255; the preview also includes released fixes through 0.0.258, notably plated-hole offset normalization. Generated SRJ records already have numeric offsets or circular geometry that ignores them. The full consumer output comparison gates that complete upgrade.

A matched local sample 16 CPU profile isolates the intended work: continuity-check time 1.767→0.528s and readable-name work 1.235→0.051s. Local route hashes match. These Bun 1.3.14 measurements supplement the actual preview-package consumer benchmarks.

Consumer RSS observations are mixed. SRJ18 sample 14 has a +10.2% median CI observation; a local pair did not reproduce growth. [The complete consumer summary](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6276015077) retains all runs, including timing slowdowns and memory outliers. There is no blanket zero-performance-regression claim. Normal build/release and an autorouter release-version dependency pin remain necessary before merging the consumer; no generated bundle or dependency patch is committed here.

title: Fix rounded SMT pad rotation on top of the visual repro
description: Fixes the rotation of rounded rectangular SMT pads to prevent merging into copper strips when CAM ignores rotation commands, ensuring accurate rendering and isolation of pads.
body:
Stacked on repro #208. Merge order: **#208 → #207**.

Rounded rectangular SMT pads relied on `%LR` to rotate their apertures. When CAM ignores this command, fine-pitch side pads merge into copper strips. Bake rotation into rounded rectangle macro coordinates for copper and soldermask, including Y reflection, while preserving exact circular corners and single-flash pad functions. Use a rotated region when a negative mask margin removes the rounded corners.

The visual test from #208 is unchanged. This PR updates its **same four 720 × 720 SVG snapshots** (top/bottom copper and soldermask), so Files Changed provides real before/after image diffs instead of adding only fixed snapshots. Fixed code against the repro snapshots fails both visual tests; updated snapshots pass.

![Before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/fix/rounded-pad-cam-rotation/tests/repros/repro12/comparison.png)

Top-copper visual diff generated with `@tscircuit/image-utils/looks-same` (magenta marks changed pixels):

![Snapshot diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/fix/rounded-pad-cam-rotation/tests/repros/repro12/snapshot-diff-top-F_Cu.png)

Visual comparison and diff generation use `@tscircuit/image-utils`; Resvg provides SVG rasterization and raw pixels for connectivity checks. The direct Sharp dependency has been removed.

Independent Gerber parsing/rasterization confirms **18 copper islands before → 32 isolated pads after**. Includes before/after Gerbers and regressions for top/bottom layers, Y reflection, mask margins, and arbitrary/negative rotations.

Validation: full suite **212 passed, 0 failed**; `tsc --noEmit` and changed TypeScript formatting passed. Repro branch independently passes 194 tests and type checking.

This is a synthetic reproduction of the suspected CAM compatibility failure, not a capture of JLC's system. The reporter's original board/parts are still needed to confirm that exact report.

title: fix: load release history only when the version dropdown opens
description: Delays loading of package release history until the version dropdown is opened, reducing initial page load time and preventing Vercel function timeouts due to slow responses from the release endpoint.
body: Opening a package currently waits for its entire release history during SSR and fetches that history again from the package page/header and editor. Slow `/package_releases/list` responses therefore delay the initial HTML and can contribute to Vercel function timeouts. Load release history when the version dropdown opens, with loading, empty, retry, and short-lived cache states. Use package metadata for the latest version and resolve explicit versions with a single release lookup. SSR fetches history only for the dedicated releases page, and lists files only for package/file/directory pages. The sidebars use the selected release's files; the editor waits for an explicitly requested release before loading its files, avoiding a transient fetch of the latest release. Opening the dropdown fetches release metadata only. Historical package files are fetched after selecting that release. The dedicated releases page continues to load history when visited. Release endpoint takes too long, so keeping this away from the initial page load

Add generic, circuit-scoped iframe tabs and update their source URL in place when the host supplies new descriptors. Add extraTabs through RunFrame, APICLI wrappers and static previews, plus standalone global injection and a change event. Preserve the selected tab and mounted iframe across ordinary view switches; safely remove tabs when their circuit no longer matches. Respect the callers availableTabs order for initial and fallback selection, while honoring an explicit default. Validate HTTP(S) descriptors and restrict the outer iframe message bridge to its real parentchild. Avoid props resync on unchanged renders and show structured-clone failures explicitly. Address the previous reviews test layout and messaging findings. Preserve the real Crisp visibility helper in an existing test mock so it cannot poison another test. Reuses and updates the work from closed 5723 on current main. No vendor assets, private viewer dependency or URL encoding is included. Validation: 81 tests pass, TypeScript and repository formatting pass, and librarystandalonestandalone-preview builds pass. A local integration with the CLI branch and a real pedometer confirms automatic URL replacement, retained tab selection and removal on mismatched circuit scope. The private viewer was tested separately for retaining its selected GPIO. Companion CLI integration: https:github.comtscircuitclipull5445 (draft pending a RunFrame release and browser-bundle update). The VercelCosmos site build also passes locally. Regression coverage verifies schematic-first tab ordering, fallback after removing an external tab, and explicit-default precedence.
body:
Hosts currently cannot add a live external configuration page beside RunFrame's built-in views. Add generic, circuit-scoped iframe tabs and update their source URL in place when the host supplies new descriptors.

- Add extraTabs through RunFrame, API/CLI wrappers and static previews, plus standalone global injection and a change event.
- Preserve the selected tab and mounted iframe across ordinary view switches; safely remove tabs when their circuit no longer matches.
- Respect the caller's availableTabs order for initial and fallback selection, while honoring an explicit default.
- Validate HTTP(S) descriptors and restrict the outer iframe message bridge to its real parent/child. Avoid props resync on unchanged renders and show structured-clone failures explicitly.
- Address the previous review's test layout and messaging findings. Preserve the real Crisp visibility helper in an existing test mock so it cannot poison another test.

Reuses and updates the work from closed #5723 on current main. No vendor assets, private viewer dependency or URL encoding is included.

Validation: 81 tests pass, TypeScript and repository formatting pass, and library/standalone/standalone-preview builds pass. A local integration with the CLI branch and a real pedometer confirms automatic URL replacement, retained tab selection and removal on mismatched circuit scope. The private viewer was tested separately for retaining its selected GPIO.

Companion CLI integration: https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5445 (draft pending a RunFrame release and browser-bundle update).

The Vercel/Cosmos site build also passes locally. Regression coverage verifies schematic-first tab ordering, fallback after removing an external tab, and explicit-default precedence.

title: perf: avoid unused DRC naming and repeated ownership checks
description: Removes unused DRC naming and repeated ownership checks in the autorouting process, optimizing performance and maintaining routing integrity.
body:
Trace-continuity DRC resolves readable names for successful traces and visits ports that its diagnostic never displays. A13 board validation also repeats obstacle/route ownership predicates. This removes that unused work while preserving routing geometry, budgets, DRC rules, error text, and ordering.

- Build both A13 connectivity views in one pass. Deduplicate only temporary predicate inputs; preserve original obstacle references, ownership metadata, order, and duplicate route names.
- Consume [checks PR #451](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/451): resolve trace names only when emitting errors and stop after the first two readable port names. First-match lookup behavior and fallback labels remain unchanged.
- Use published `@tscircuit/checks@^0.0.259`, which includes merged [checks PR #451](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/451), in place of the CI preview. This includes released changes since the base's 0.0.255, including plated-hole offset normalization. Generated SRJ offsets are already numeric or unused by circular geometry. The output comparisons below were run against the earlier preview of the same naming optimization.

Validation:
- Release dependency update `d227d5a` replaces only the checks preview URL with `^0.0.259`; fresh autorouter CI is running. The benchmark and artifact results below remain measurements of preview head `9992658`.
- Autorouter CI is fully green on `9992658`, including Format Check, type checking, both builds, all nine Bun shards, dependency-patch and ID-hack checks, and Vercel.
- Checks PR #451 is fully green, including full tests and packed-consumer checks.
- Local formatting, build, type checking, and 13 focused DRC/ownership tests pass with the actual preview.
- Four long bug-report tests pass with 5,519 assertions and unchanged snapshots for reports 94, 96, and 103.
- [Independent artifact comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/39314701247) passes for all seven benchmark pairs: **329 paired records covering 127 unique inputs and 321 SVG pairs**. Every completed-board SVG is byte-identical; all routing, DRC messages, via counts, lint counts, and search metrics match. Seven existing dataset 24 timeout error strings differ only in heartbeat iteration/progress numbers. Those raw differences were retained separately; timeout status, duration, phase, solver, and all other fields match. Whole timeout records are not claimed byte-identical.

All revised benchmarks ran after CI was green, on unchanged base `bc19466` versus head `9992658`: Pipeline 9, effort 1, concurrency 4, eight logical ARM64 CPUs, Bun 1.4.2, one thread per sample, and a fresh process per board. No benchmark harness or solver budget changes. Negative timing deltas are faster; stage times are summed work across boards.

| Dataset/run | P50 | P95 | Total stage time | Joint DRC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [18 / 1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275185028) | +1.3% | −8.6% | −3.78% | −13.28% |
| [18 / 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275296473) | −8.2% | −3.4% | −5.43% | −13.09% |
| [18 / 3](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275298764) | −2.4% | −4.1% | −1.97% | −10.05% |
| [1 / 1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275189982) | +2.9% | +1.3% | +0.85% | −4.62% |
| [1 / 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275447654) | −1.3% | −7.0% | −2.87% | −20.43% |
| [1 / 3](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275450765) | −10.2% | −3.0% | −4.41% | −16.76% |
| [24](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6275187897) | −6.0% | unchanged, timeout-capped | −1.31% | −5.35% |

Dataset 18's three pairs were fixed before any revised dataset 18 result. Dataset 1's two additional pairs were fixed after its first slower result. All results are retained; no further repeats were selected.

The strongest evidence is dataset 18 joint DRC: combined time falls **12.19%**, accounting for **87.8% of net stage savings**, while combined high-density routing is flat (−0.03%). All three runs reduce total stage work. Gains concentrate in long boards: samples 12 and 15 are faster in every pair. Dataset 1's small overall differences overlap drift in unaffected stages; no substantial gain is established there. Dataset 24's 18 completed boards use about 4.8% less cumulative solve time in this one pair; its seven existing timeouts, eight failed boards, and two DRC issues remain unchanged. Its P80–P95 stay capped at 360 s.

**Memory remains an open observation, so this is not a blanket claim of zero performance regressions.** Dataset 18 sample 14's median RSS is 325.6 MiB higher (+10.2%), with increases in two of three pairs. Dataset 24 also has mixed RSS outliers, including on a timeout before changed routing stages execute. A separate local serial sample 14 pair did not reproduce growth (−0.62% RSS, identical output), but uses Bun 1.3.14. Retain the CI memory observations for review before merging; no forced GC or cache/budget workaround was added.

A matched local sample 16 CPU profile supports the intended cause: continuity-check time 1.767→0.528s and readable-name work 1.235→0.051s. These local measurements supplement the complete consumer benchmarks above.

<details>
<summary>Previous ownership-only candidate, retained for comparison</summary>

Head `93da532` did not establish a stable dataset speedup. These results must not be attributed to the revised checks dependency.

| Dataset/run | P50 | P95 | Total stage time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6273139057) | −1.6% | +1.4% | −1.12% |
| [18 / first](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6273134107) | +9.0% | +3.0% | +6.65% |
| [18 / additional](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6274193342) | −3.1% | −1.5% | −3.52% |
| [18 / diagnostic repeat](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6274370270) | +1.7% | +1.7% | −0.18% |
| [24](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3139#issuecomment-6273136789) | −1.3% | unchanged, timeout-capped | +0.03% |

Recorded routing outcomes were unchanged. Raw comparisons of the original first dataset 1/18/24 runs covered 127 matched boards and 119 byte-identical completed-board SVGs.

</details>

title: Speed up rectdiff with shared edge projections and expansion query reuse
description: Updates the rectdiff Git dependency to improve performance by sharing sorted projections and reusing rectangle-expansion queries, resulting in reduced processing times without altering routing outcomes.
body:
Update the rectdiff Git dependency from `215284c` to `d3a8b095035f4e7d03cdb19f2fdb7a554c6c008a` from [rectdiff PR164](https://github.com/tscircuit/rectdiff/pull/164). The consumer diff is one dependency hash.

The weak original benchmark signal had two causes: the index-only implementation still rebuilt and sorted blocker intervals for each aligned edge, and topology accounts for only about 1–2% of the larger datasets' recorded pipeline time. The updated algorithm shares sorted projections per exact line and reuses completed rectangle-expansion queries. It preserves candidate order, clipping, raw distance ranking and float representation.

Final-head Blacksmith benchmarks, each running both revisions sequentially on the same machine with Pipeline9, effort 1 and concurrency 4:

| Dataset | Topology stage, base → PR | Less topology time | Sum of recorded stages, base → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135#issuecomment-6285068668), 85 boards | 11.771 → 10.527 s | 10.6% | 257.227 → 249.890 s (−2.9%) |
| [18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135#issuecomment-6285066534), 16 boards | 11.638 → 9.160 s | 21.3% | 1120.025 → 1124.449 s (+0.4%) |
| [24](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135#issuecomment-6285067417), 26 boards | 69.638 → 50.852 s | 27.0% | 3773.391 → 3742.969 s (−0.8%) |

The last column sums recorded stage times, including partial stages in failed/timed-out samples; it is not a component-only measurement. Dataset24's seven existing 360-second timeouts cap its higher timing percentiles. Dataset24 P50 routing time improves 87.1→80.4 s (−7.7%), while P60 increases 159.8→170.5 s (+6.7%). All three datasets report **zero routing-outcome changes**, with unchanged via/angled-trace averages and DRC counts. Datasets01/18 have all boards complete without DRC issues; dataset24 retains its existing 18/26 completions, seven timeouts and two DRC issues.

Rectdiff-only solve measurements isolate the change:

| Rectdiff workload | Original `215284c` | Final `d3a8b09` | Less solve time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01, 85 boards | 2.237 s | 1.767 s | 21.0% |
| dataset18, 16 boards | 5.823 s | 4.372 s | 24.9% |
| dataset24, 26 boards | 32.447 s | 21.207 s | 34.6% |
| bugreport109 | 93.970 s | 5.384 s | 94.3% |

Local Linux x64, Bun 1.3.14, same host and inputs, `RectDiffPipeline` with `maxGapFillPasses: 4`. One warmup per revision followed by two ABBA cycles: four measured passes per revision. Values are means of summed `solve()` time across each workload. Input cloning, explicit GC and output hashing are outside the timed solve; every pass verifies the complete ordered mesh JSON hash.

| Full Pipeline9 board109 | Original dependency | Updated dependency | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Topology time | 94.728 s | 5.948 s | 93.7% |
| Full solve time | 459.909 s | 382.218 s | 16.9% |
| Mean peak routing RSS | 2595.6 MiB | 2536.6 MiB | 2.3% |

Board109 uses fresh-process full Pipeline9 ABBA runs on the same Linux x64 host, Bun 1.3.14, effort 1 and `cacheProvider: null`: two processes per revision. All four complete routed-JSON hashes match, with all 349 endpoint pairs routed, 349 traces, 414 vias and zero relaxed DRC errors. Input, resolved dependency source and Git revisions are audited in every process.

Validation at `2a436ee` / `d3a8b09`:

- [Consumer CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135/checks) and [upstream CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/rectdiff/pull/164/checks) are green, including all nine consumer test shards, build, types, formatting, dependency checks and Vercel deployment.
- 110 local rectdiff tests pass, one existing skip; existing SVG snapshots unchanged.
- Complete ordered mesh JSON matches the original dependency for all 127 dataset01/18/24 boards plus board109. All 119 completed final benchmark SVGs match their baseline byte-for-byte.
- Independent exact comparisons cover 30,000 ordered edge inputs and 1,500 expansion inputs. Focused regression coverage includes negative width, height and both for obstacles and hard placements. Ranking-index bounds remain conservative while exact distances use the original rectangles.

Full-pipeline RAM results are mixed. Dataset24's final P50/P80/P90 peak RSS improve 4.8%/1.5%/4.8%, but dataset18 P50 increases 6.9%, and dataset24 sample 010 increases 679.3→775.7 MiB (+14.2%) in the official ARM run. Separate fresh-process ABBA checks under Bun 1.4.2/x64 preserve identical routes and measure about 2.6% higher mean peak RSS for samples 010 and 020; the larger gaps appear downstream after topology. Source review found no new persistent cache/index retention path, but does not establish the cause. These measurements remain a limitation: no universal memory-parity or per-board overall-time claim is made.

title: fix: preserve physical footprint classification in PCB exports (#585)
description: Fixes PCB exports to preserve physical footprint classification, ensuring KiCads 3D Viewer correctly identifies SMD and through-hole parts based on exported pad types.
body:
PCB exports omit footprint type attributes, causing KiCad's 3D Viewer to classify physical SMD and through-hole parts as virtual. Infer the missing type from the exported pads: plated `thru_hole` pads take precedence, otherwise use `smd`. Explicit metadata types and existing exclusion/DNP flags are preserved.

Stacked on #702. Fixes #585.

The same small helper is used for component footprints, standalone SMD/plated-hole footprints, and extracted library footprints. Exact pad-type comparisons also stop non-plated mounting holes from classifying an SMD footprint as through-hole. Three existing library text snapshots and one PCB fixture change only that attribute.

The TSX repro now passes as a normal test. Added focused coverage for mixed pads and exclusions, and extended existing tests for explicit metadata overrides and non-plated holes. No drawing or image-snapshot changes.

Validation:
- Full GitHub Actions test suite passes with native KiCad 10.0.1.
- 20 relevant PCB, library, and metadata tests pass with the repository's existing CI settings.
- Formatting, TypeScript checks, and build pass.
- The stricter local PNG comparison has an existing mismatch reproduced unchanged on main; no PNG snapshots or thresholds were modified.

description: Aligned edges previously repeated blocker clipping and sorting after each spatial lookup. body:
Aligned edges previously repeated blocker clipping and sorting after each spatial lookup. This change shares sorted projections per exact line, reuses completed rectangle-expansion queries, maintains full-stack blockers incrementally, and avoids allocating layer intersections for rectangles that do not overlap. Edge tasks use traversal ordinals so shared work preserves the original candidate precedence and float representation.

Rectdiff-only solve measurements at `d3a8b09`:

| Rectdiff workload | Original `215284c` | Final `d3a8b09` | Less solve time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01, 85 boards | 2.237 s | 1.767 s | 21.0% |
| dataset18, 16 boards | 5.823 s | 4.372 s | 24.9% |
| dataset24, 26 boards | 32.447 s | 21.207 s | 34.6% |
| bugreport109 | 93.970 s | 5.384 s | 94.3% |

Local Linux x64, Bun 1.3.14, same host and inputs, `RectDiffPipeline` with `maxGapFillPasses: 4`. One warmup per revision, then two ABBA cycles: four measured passes per revision. Values are means of summed `solve()` time across each workload. Input cloning, explicit GC and output hashing are outside the timed solve; every pass verifies the complete ordered mesh JSON hash.

| Full Pipeline9 board109 | Original dependency | Updated dependency | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Topology time | 94.728 s | 5.948 s | 93.7% |
| Full solve time | 459.909 s | 382.218 s | 16.9% |
| Mean peak routing RSS | 2595.6 MiB | 2536.6 MiB | 2.3% |

Board109 uses fresh-process full Pipeline9 ABBA runs on the same Linux x64 host, Bun 1.3.14, effort 1 and `cacheProvider: null`: two processes per revision. All four complete routed-JSON hashes match, with all 349 endpoint pairs routed, 349 traces, 414 vias and zero relaxed DRC errors. Each process audits its input, resolved rectdiff source and Git revisions.

Validation at `d3a8b09`:

- 110 tests pass, one existing skip; existing SVG snapshots unchanged. Local types, build and formatting pass. [Upstream CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/rectdiff/pull/164/checks) and [consumer CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135/checks), including all nine consumer test shards, are green.
- Complete ordered mesh JSON matches the original `215284c` dependency for all 127 dataset01/18/24 boards plus board109.
- Independent exact comparisons pass for 30,000 ordered edge-candidate arrays and 1,500 expansion inputs, including tiny/reversed extents, missing layers and signed zero.
- A regression test covers negative width, height and both for obstacles and hard placements. Only ranking-index box bounds are canonicalized; exact distances still use the original raw rectangles.
- The expansion regression fixture emits the same 6×6 rectangle with 11 searches per layer instead of 80.

[Consumer PR3135](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135) pins this revision at `2a436ee`. Final same-machine Pipeline9 benchmarks were run after all CI checks passed: [dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135#issuecomment-6285068668), [dataset18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135#issuecomment-6285066534), [dataset24](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3135#issuecomment-6285067417). Topology time is lower by 10.6%, 21.3% and 27.0%, respectively, with zero routing-outcome changes. Because topology accounts for roughly 1–2% of the latter datasets, those gains produce much smaller overall-routing changes. Dataset24 still has its existing seven timeouts and two DRC issues.

Full-pipeline RAM results are mixed. Dataset24's final P50/P80/P90 peak RSS improve 4.8%/1.5%/4.8%, but dataset18 P50 increases 6.9%, and dataset24 sample 010 increases 679.3→775.7 MiB (+14.2%) in the official ARM run. Separate fresh-process ABBA checks under Bun 1.4.2/x64 preserve identical routes and measure about 2.6% higher mean peak RSS for samples 010 and 020; the larger gaps appear downstream after topology. Source review found no new persistent cache/index retention path, but does not establish the cause. These measurements remain a limitation: no universal memory-parity or per-board overall-time claim is made.

title: chore: update circuit-json-to-kicad dependency and bundled types
description: Updates the circuit-json-to-kicad development dependency to version 0.0.241 and regenerates TypeScript declarations to include missing API methods, enhancing type safety for users.
body:
Update the `circuit-json-to-kicad` development dependency from 0.0.137 to 0.0.241, regenerate its bundled TypeScript declarations, and extend the importer’s compile-time coverage.

## Motivation

The existing declaration snapshot omits `CircuitJsonToKicadSchConverter.getOutputFiles()`. Consumers calling this API through the typed importer receive `TS2339`, even when the loaded converter supports multi-file schematic output. Refreshing the snapshot makes those declarations available to consumers.

The default CDN resolver already requests `latest` for unversioned imports. This is a dependency and declaration maintenance update; it does not change converter implementation or runtime version selection.

## Before

- The development dependency and bundled KiCad declarations use 0.0.137.
- `getOutputFiles({ schematicFilename: "board.kicad_sch" })` fails type-checking because the declaration is missing.

## After

- The development dependency is 0.0.241, and the KiCad declaration bundle is regenerated from that published package.
- The importer exposes the multi-file schematic method, its options, and its file-output types.
- A compile-time check verifies the output shape and rejects a non-string root filename.

## Related merged work

Version 0.0.241 contains [tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad#673](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/pull/673), which fixed `Max iterations reached` on PCB exports with 1,000 or more traces by scaling the iteration budget. The CLI adopted that release in [tscircuit/cli#5463](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5463). These are related upstream changes; this PR updates the importer’s development dependency and declarations.

## Validation

- The new compile-time check fails against the previous declarations and passes after regeneration.
- `bun test`: 23 passed, 0 failed.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The regenerated KiCad bundle exactly matches the installed 0.0.241 declarations; no other type bundles changed.

title: fix: analyze four-pin crystal load capacitor placement
description: Fixes the issue where four-pin crystals were skipped in the crystal placement analyzer, ensuring correct detection and reporting of their load capacitor placements.
body: ## Motivation The crystal placement analyzer only considered components with exactly two ports, so it skipped four-pin crystals even when their two oscillator nets had the usual load capacitors. Four-pin crystals also use their extra pins for the grounded case, so moving them vertically onto the capacitor pins would make a correct schematic worse. Repro: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/pull/129 ## What changed - Detects the two oscillator nets of a `simple_crystal` from circuit connectivity while excluding its grounded case pins. - Reports a four-pin crystal only when it is horizontally off-center between its two load capacitors. - Preserves the crystal's vertical placement; the suggested correction changes only `schX`. - Keeps the existing two-port fallback for legacy `simple_chip` crystal data without enabling multi-port chip detection. - Adds a corrected snapshot with complete C31/C32 connections and a clean U13-to-crystal ground path, and verifies that it emits no placement issues. - Keeps already-centered real-board crystals unchanged. ## Before, detected, and corrected | Before — four-pin crystal is skipped | Detected — horizontal correction | Corrected — same topology, centered crystal | | --- | --- | --- | | No `CrystalNotCenteredOverLoadCapacitors` issue is emitted. | Y2, C31, and C32 are identified; the suggestion preserves Y2's vertical position. | Y2 is horizontally centered, the capacitor and ground connections remain complete, and the analyzer reports zero issues. | | | | | Reference: [Renesas 8V41NS0412 Evaluation Board User Guide, Figure 5 on page 10](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/mah/8v41ns0412-evaluation-board-user-guide) ## Validation - 187 tests pass - Type-checking passes - Formatting passes

title: Detect separated transistor resistor misalignment
description: Detects misalignment between a transistor and its connected resistor in circuit schematics, ensuring proper alignment for electrical connectivity.
body:
R12 in the ESP32 GPS tracker's PWRKEY network is separated from Q1 with perpendicular connected terminals. `TransistorResistorAlignmentSolver` now emits `TransistorResistorNotAligned` for separated, private non-rail connections between a typed resistor and BJT that cannot read as a straight facing connection.

Stack: #326 (TSX repro) → this solver PR. Merge the repro first. This stack is independent of the potentiometer stack.

![Tracker resistor and transistor before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/2dfa177cf0ca0d950b67403fe80cbc677662554e/tests/cases/__snapshots__/transistor-resistor-alignment-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The TSX proof comes from [pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker v1.1.0](https://tscircuit.com/pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker?version=1.1.0#schematic). The correction rotates Q1, moves R12 onto its connected terminal's axis and rotates/repositions R13 to correct its existing rail-orientation warning. Native symbols, values and source electrical records are preserved. Tests verify continuous drawn R12–Q1 and R13–Q1 wires as well as electrical connectivity. Full analysis of the complete three-part extract reports zero findings. The original repro and a separate full corrected network snapshot are retained; this is not a claim that the entire published board is clean.

The rule uses existing `simple_transistor` NPN/PNP and `simple_resistor` metadata, connectivity and drawn terminal directions. It does not infer base/collector/emitter roles from names or pin numbers, so it applies to either transistor polarity without a fixed terminal order. It accepts horizontal or vertical straight connections and small local bends. The separation threshold is the larger of 2 schematic units or twice the resistor's largest dimension; straight facing connections allow 0.15 units of lateral tolerance. It skips branched/shared nets, rail-connected resistors, feedback to another terminal of the same transistor, overlapping bodies, separate sheets/groups, DNP/DNC and ambiguous geometry.

Existing coverage: `LowSideTransistorPlacementSolver` requires a particular clamped-load network, which this tracker does not have. Its load-position/orientation finding and the new resistor-alignment finding are independent: both are reported when applicable, including when requesting only the new issue type. `TransistorRailOrientationSolver` handles supply/ground resistor branches. The current component-pin rule needs multiple qualifying pin connections, and #282's proposed single-pair extension still requires already-horizontal facing terminals. Neither covers this perpendicular R12/Q1 connection. [SIM800 Hardware Design, Figure 10](https://simcom.ee/documents/SIM800/SIM800_Hardware%20Design_V1.09.pdf#page=22) shows the same resistor-fed transistor PWRKEY arrangement.

Four existing fixture snapshots gain diagnostics without changing their schematic components or traces: the PNP orientation fixture also has a misaligned input resistor R3; the low-side scope fixture has a misaligned R1/Q1 pair even when semantic terminal aliases are absent; and the STM32 and low-side-driver fixtures now report resistor alignment alongside their independent load-position/orientation finding. Tests assert that the new alignment finding is retained in both full and filtered analysis.

Validation: all 266 tests pass, plus typecheck, build and formatting. Guard tests cover renamed pins/nets, branched/feedback/rail connections, missing/duplicate geometry, scope, rotation/reflection and alignment tolerance. Both correction SVGs were rendered and visually inspected. No dependency, schema or timeout changes.

description: Detects capacitors that are not properly placed next to their corresponding resistor-divider taps in the schematic, ensuring correct component placement for improved circuit functionality.
body:
C_AMP_L/R in the published pocket-audio-player input network are separated from their resistor-divider taps. `ResistorDividerCapacitorPlacementSolver` now emits `CapacitorSeparatedFromResistorDivider` for each channel. Rotating only the two ground-connected resistors leaves both new findings; moving the capacitors beside their divider taps produces a visibly connected six-part network with zero full-analysis findings.

Stack: #320 (real-board TSX repro) → this PR. Merge #320 first. This stack is independent of #318/#319.

![Before and after: complete left input network](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/56d923b81457d2dbde00f68bf71804dc9b7958c6/tests/cases/__snapshots__/resistor-divider-capacitor-correction-comparison-l.snap.svg)

The original stereo network has two existing resistor-orientation findings plus two new capacitor-separation findings. Each channel has its own comparison so the drawing remains readable: [right-channel comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/56d923b81457d2dbde00f68bf71804dc9b7958c6/tests/cases/__snapshots__/resistor-divider-capacitor-correction-comparison-r.snap.svg). The [complete corrected stereo network](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/56d923b81457d2dbde00f68bf71804dc9b7958c6/tests/cases/__snapshots__/resistor-divider-capacitor-correction-full-network.snap.svg) contains all six parts. This is a functional-network extract from [Devesh36/pocket-audio-player v1.0.12](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/pocket-audio-player?version=1.0.12#schematic), not a full-board correction.

Detection requires a non-rail node containing exactly two typed resistors and one capacitor, with exactly one resistor grounded at its other end. The capacitor's shared pin must be distant from both resistor pins. The rule skips extra branches, unavailable geometry, unpopulated parts, capacitors bridging the input resistor and possible feedback returning to the same chip. It uses typed metadata and connectivity, with no name-based role inference. This reports a placement suggestion; it does not move components automatically.

[TI TLV320AIC3206, Figure 23, page 38](https://www.ti.com/lit/gpn/tlv320aic3206#page=38) shows the corresponding divider-tap/coupling-capacitor topology. The rule's spacing allowance is a schematic-readability heuristic, not a TI electrical or PCB requirement.

- Tests verify unchanged electrical records, continuous drawn wires, both corrected channels and the complete corrected network reporting zero issues. An orientation-only correction still reports both capacitor-separation findings.

Source: [techmannih/nema34-mounted-stepper-controller v0.3.92](https://tscircuit.com/techmannih/nema34-mounted-stepper-controller?version=0.3.92#schematic), release `f9c7a51c-0362-489e-94d3-5901eb27ba81`, `index.circuit.tsx`.

The fixture includes all four parts in this voltage-monitor network: R31, R32, R33 and C24. It retains their published positions, orientations, values, pin connections and explicit net metadata. The surrounding board is omitted at the named boundary nets; this is a functional-network extract, not a full-board repro. The fixture also provides a corrected placement variant for the solver tests. Circuit JSON is generated from TSX using the current dependencies.

body:
Preserve the exact first-byte native input that timed out after 30 minutes / 572,200 steps: 11 signals, 1,144 obstacles, no supplied copper, 0.50/0.30 mm full-through vias, TOP/BOTTOM cohorts and the original 33.585277–34.220277 mm length window. Compressed/raw SHA-256 checks prevent fixture changes.

Core passes this valid first-phase SRJ directly to bus-lanes; no earlier-phase traces or capacity-autorouter conversion are involved. The headless baseline also stalls: 60 seconds / 11,364 steps, attempt 6, 5,515 visibility vertices. At 11 fixed-layer signals, negotiation is disabled: one DQS corridor stays locked while ordinary-lane orders retry against it.

The fast regression compares the original input with a redundant global TOP/BOTTOM restriction. Per-bus restrictions already constrain all signals to those layers, but the two select different routing stages. It intentionally fails on main (`lanes_coupled_pairs` versus `route_shared_layers`). The bounded CLI runs searches serially without waiting 30 minutes.

A diagnostic independent-bus strategy routed 11 candidate carriers within both length windows in about 16 seconds / 6,640 steps, then failed the physical exterior-coupling check (about 2.04 mm edge gap versus 0.140 mm allowed). This is rejected intermediate geometry, not a completed route. The fixture notes record the verified search behavior and further native-pad pair-tuning hypotheses. No production changes or partial-route images are included.

Run `bun test tests/am3352-byte-stall-layer-dispatch.test.ts` or `bun scripts/repro-am3352-byte-stall.ts --case both --steps 12000 --seconds 60`.

body:
The exact native AM3352 11-signal byte capture from #62 now completes in **16.8 seconds / 5,222 steps**, instead of timing out after 30 minutes. Its 1,144 obstacles, original pads, layer assignments, timing windows, DQS coupling constraints, and 0.50 mm land / 0.30 mm full-through drills are unchanged.

Stacked on #62 (`repro/am3352-byte-routing-stall`). Integration with main includes the already merged #61.

The solver negotiates independent fixed-layer buses, joins coupled approaches into owned native package pads, and tries an equal-length alternative shared-centerline bend when the first corridor blocks ordinary signals. Request-local memoization and pair-route exclusions avoid repeating identical failed searches. Stable bend ties and joint package-entry repair apply to fresh native pads; existing fanout handoffs retain their established ordering and geometry. All copper is generated from the original input, without saved route guides.

Validation:

- Exact capture: all 11 connections, both whole-copper length windows, DQS skew and exterior coupling, copper/drill/NPTH clearance, board edges, unchanged nontrace geometry, and all twelve 0.30 mm drills pass independent checks. Snapshot export rejects incomplete or invalid output.
- CI: 484 tests pass, plus formatting, types, package validation and preview. Local integration with merged main passes all 486 tests.
- Fresh strict legacy placement proof, updated solver plus merged #61: **11/11 solved**, each with all 47 connections, independent native DRC, full-copper bus/pair matching and physical coupling. One-hour-per-case limit; longest `control-inner1` 1,590.859 s, `outer-layers` 955.370 s; total solver time 3,643.172 s. All input hashes and all 161 fixed power fanouts per sample are preserved. All eleven fresh routed snapshots were inspected.
- The earlier 180-second comparison remains available as historical evidence: six accepted cases and five timeouts. No solver, fixture or constraint changes were made for the long-budget proof.

[Fresh 11/11 proof, measurements and route images](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/8efb7acc6ba9e7e19dcd8ce30dde326afedd9ea0/docs/routed-am3352-byte/legacy-full-proof/README.md) · [Validated native byte route](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/8efb7acc6ba9e7e19dcd8ce30dde326afedd9ea0/docs/routed-am3352-byte/README.md) · [Earlier bounded placement comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/8efb7acc6ba9e7e19dcd8ce30dde326afedd9ea0/docs/routed-am3352-byte/legacy-placement-comparison.md)

This validates the captured byte phase; the complete SBC has not been rerouted in this PR.

title: Avoid duplicate CI runs for pull request branches
description: Restricts push-triggered workflows to the main branch, preventing duplicate CI runs for pull request branches.
body:
Restrict push-triggered renderer and parity workflows to `main`. Pull requests still run both workflows, and the parity workflow retains its manual trigger. Updating an open repository PR no longer starts a second identical workflow from the feature-branch push.

Validation: parsed both workflows and checked the main-only push filters, preserved pull-request triggers, and preserved manual parity trigger. `git diff --check` passes.

title: Simplify test discovery and formatting scripts
description: Replaces the hand-maintained test filename list with automatic discovery under tests, excluding generated upstream and actual trees, while formatting source and test directories without duplicating filename lists.
body:
Replace the hand-maintained test filename list with discovery under `tests`, excluding the generated `upstream` and `actual` trees. New nested tests are picked up automatically while the separate reference-test command remains unchanged.

Format the source and test directories instead of duplicating filename lists in both formatting scripts. Explicit Biome exclusions preserve generated upstream files, actual output, snapshots, and JSON fixtures.

Validation:

- `bun run test`: all 92 tests pass.
- A temporary nested test is discovered, while deliberately failing tests in the generated directories are excluded.
- Invalid temporary fixture/snapshot JSON does not enter the formatter.
- `bun run format:check`, `bun run typecheck`, and `git diff --check` pass.

title: refactor: share WebGPU browser launch configuration
description: Centralizes Chromiums WebGPU launch options in launchWebGpuBrowser, shared by visual tests, teardrop test, parity renderer, and rendering CLI.
body:
Centralize Chromium's WebGPU launch options in `launchWebGpuBrowser`, shared by the visual tests, teardrop test, parity renderer, and rendering CLI. The helper preserves headless operation, software-rendering flags, and `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE` support.

Validation:

- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Verified default, software-rendering, and custom-executable launch configurations.
- `WEBGPU_SOFTWARE=1 bun run test:visual`: all 24 snapshots pass.
- `WEBGPU_SOFTWARE=1 bun run test:teardrops` passes.
- The rendering CLI produces a 400×300 PCB render with zero diagnostics using the shared helper.

title: Reduce dense-board via tessellation
description: Adds a renderViasInHighDetail setting to reduce excessive WebGPU geometry for large boards by targeting a 0.0025 mm chord error without exceeding the previous 96-segment resolution.
body:
Large boards generate excessive WebGPU geometry because every via uses 96 segments.

This adds a `renderViasInHighDetail` setting. High detail remains the default; disabling it targets 0.0025 mm chord error without exceeding the previous 96-segment resolution.

Includes dense visual coverage for tented, untented, and buried inner-layer vias.

title: Check formatting in renderer CI
description: Run the existing format:check script in the renderer workflow immediately after installing dependencies to ensure formatting drift fails CI before the build and browser checks.
body:
Run the existing `format:check` script in the renderer workflow immediately after installing dependencies. Formatting drift now fails CI before the build and browser checks.

Validation: `bun run format:check` passes; the workflow parses successfully and `git diff --check` is clean.

title: Deduplicate OCCT assets and verify offline 3D STEP rendering
description: Deduplicates OCCT assets to reduce payload size and adds verification for offline 3D STEP rendering in the viewer.
body:
The standalone embedded OCCT's loader and 7.6 MB WASM twice: once for exporters and once at the viewer's versioned CDN paths. Route the viewer through a small local wrapper that shares the exporters' loader/WASM and overrides the caller's CDN locateFile callback. This removes about 7.7 MB of duplicate payload while retaining relative URLs for nested sites.

Add a generated STEP solid to compiled-binary qualification. The browser check parses real STEP geometry, opens the actual dev 3D viewer, waits for both the board and STEP mesh, checks canonical OCCT requests, and rejects external request attempts. CI runs it in its existing loopback-only network namespace.

Validation:
- Rebuilt JS CDN and native macOS arm64 executable; each complete OCCT payload occurs exactly once in the executable.
- Root and UI typechecks pass.
- Full test suite: 168 pass, 0 fail (GNU tar on PATH), run in the localhost-only sandbox.
- Compiled build/site/dev/browser smoke passes under a macOS OS sandbox permitting localhost connections only; a public-IP connection is rejected with EPERM.
- Actual dev 3D board and STEP rendering: zero external request attempts and no page errors, with a fresh browser context and service workers blocked.
- OCCT initialization and STEP parsing pass at dev and nested static-site module URLs.
- Baked datasheet files match the existing release snapshot byte for byte.

Known limitation: the full exported-site HTML has pre-existing Tailwind and eval-version network lookups. The offline rendering qualification here covers tsci dev; nested-site qualification covers the OCCT module/WASM paths.

title: Update CLI and share one Manifold 3.5.1 runtime
description: Pins the CLI commit and uses one Manifold 3.5.1 loaderWASM pair for the viewer and exporters, ensuring compatibility and passing all tests.
body:
Pin the CLI commit from https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5488 and use one Manifold `3.5.1` loader/WASM pair for the viewer and exporters. The viewer's versioned URL re-exports the shared loader.

The compiled binary passes `tsci dev`, site copying, 3D preview and FDM export checks in a loopback-only sandbox, at both dev and nested static-site URLs. UI/binary builds and type checks pass; 166 tests pass, with two local archive tests requiring GNU tar on macOS.
